definition_zh: 种子；起源；选手排名；播种
definition_en: a small object from which a plant grows; the cause or beginning of something; to rank players in a tournament
core_image: 一粒小种子埋进土里，悄悄决定未来整株植物的模样
scene: 春天到了，农妇蹲在田里准备下种。 Every seed in this packet will grow into a sunflower.
sceneCN: 这里 seed 是「种子」（第 1 个义项：能长成植物的颗粒）；句意是这包里的每粒种子都会长成向日葵。

derivatives.zh: seed 加 -y 形容词后缀，义为「结籽的；破旧的；可疑的」
seed 加 -ling 名词后缀，义为「幼苗」
seed 的过去分词形容词用法，义为「已播种的；（选手）列为种子的」

senses.title: A grain that grows into a plant
senses.definition: a small hard part of a plant that can grow into a new plant
senses.definitionCN: 植物体内能长出新植株的小颗粒
senses.example: She saved seeds from the best tomatoes.
senses.exampleCN: 她把最好的番茄留了种。
senses.why: The tiny buried kernel silently holds the whole future plant.
senses.whyCN: 埋进土里的小颗粒悄悄装着未来整株植物。

senses.title: The beginning or hidden cause of something
senses.definition: the start or hidden cause of a feeling, idea, or event
senses.definitionCN: 情感、想法或事件的起点或隐藏诱因
senses.example: The defeat planted the seed of reform.
senses.exampleCN: 这场失败埋下了改革的种子。
senses.why: What fits in a grain can later fill a field — causes start small.
senses.whyCN: 一粒之内的东西日后能占满一整片田——起因总是从微小开始。

senses.title: A ranked player in a tournament
senses.definition: a player given a ranking so strong rivals do not meet early
senses.definitionCN: 在赛事中被排定名次、避免强者过早相遇的选手
senses.example: The top seed won every round easily.
senses.exampleCN: 头号种子轻松赢下每一轮。
senses.why: The ranked players are pre-planted in fixed positions, like seeds in rows.
senses.whyCN: 被排名的选手像成排的种子一样被预先安置在固定位置。

senses.title: To put seeds in the ground
senses.definition: to place seeds in soil so plants will grow
senses.definitionCN: 把种子放进土壤以便生长
senses.example: They seeded the field with wheat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在田里播下了小麦。
senses.why: The grain becomes a verb: you do the planting yourself.
senses.whyCN: 颗粒变成动词：由你亲手完成栽种。

senses.title: Seeds or pits of fruit
senses.definition: the small hard parts inside a fruit
senses.definitionCN: 果实内部细小的硬粒
senses.example: Remove the seeds before blending the melon.
senses.exampleCN: 打瓜汁前先把籽去掉。
senses.why: The same kernel hides inside the sweet flesh.
senses.whyCN: 同样的硬粒藏在甜美的果肉里。

intro.en: From Old English saed, related to sowing.
intro.cn: 来自古英语 saed，与「播种」相关。

items.en: The reconstructed root *sehi- means to sow or scatter.
items.cn: 重构词根 *sehi- 意为「播撒」。

items.en: Germanic forms gave both sow and seed from the same idea of scattering.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式从「播撒」这一意象同时产出 sow 与 seed。

items.en: Old English saed meant what is sown: the seed itself.
items.cn: 古英语 saed 意为「被播撒之物」，即种子。

items.en: The spelling became seed, with the double vowel marking length.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写演变为 seed，双元音标记长音。

items.en: Modern use adds beginnings of ideas, ranked players, and the verb to sow.
items.cn: 现代用法新增「起因」「种子选手」及动词「播种」。

note.en: Look-alikes in the seed spelling family, and near words in the beginning field.
note.cn: seed 拼写家族的形近词，以及「开端」义场的近义词。

entries.definition: to look for something
entries.definitionCN: 寻找——与 seed 仅差词尾一个字母，注意区分

entries.definition: shabby and unpleasant
entries.definitionCN: 破旧的；可疑的——由 seed 派生，注意词义转移

entries.definition: to give food to
entries.definitionCN: 喂食——拼写与 seed 相近但词源不同

entries.definition: the point where something starts
entries.definitionCN: 起源——抽象用法近义，seed 更具画面感

entries.definition: where something comes from
entries.definitionCN: 来源——强调出处，seed 强调孕育未来的潜能

entries.definition: the central part of a nut or idea
entries.definitionCN: 核心——与果核义项相近，kernel 更抽象

normalIntro.en: Hooks on planting, spelling neighbors, and the tournament bracket.
normalIntro.cn: 基于播种、拼写邻居与赛事对阵表的记忆钩子。

normal.en: sow and seed share the same ancient root of scattering
normal.cn: sow 与 seed 共享古老的「播撒」词根

normal.en: seed of doubt: a feeling that grows like a plant
normal.cn: seed of doubt：像植物一样生长的情绪

normal.en: top seed sits at the top of the bracket like a planted row
normal.cn: 头号种子像成排种下的作物，被安置在对阵表顶端

normal.en: go to seed means the plant has finished and faded
normal.cn: go to seed 表示植物结籽后走向凋零

normal.en: seedling is the baby form, -ling marks smallness
normal.cn: seedling 是「幼苗」，后缀 -ling 标记幼小

abstract.en: Picture pressing one tiny grain into dark soil
abstract.cn: 想象把一粒小小的种子按进黑土

abstract.en: See a doubt growing quietly into a tall thorn bush
abstract.cn: 看见一点疑心悄悄长成高高的荆棘

abstract.en: Feel the tournament chart as a field with fixed rows
abstract.cn: 把对阵表想象成分好行的田地

examples.en: The wind carried the seeds across the valley.
examples.cn: 风把种子吹过山谷。

examples.en: Their argument planted a seed of doubt in my mind.
examples.cn: 他们的争论在我心里埋下了怀疑的种子。

examples.en: She is the second seed in this tournament.
examples.cn: 她是本次赛事的二号种子选手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「西的」——种子是西方传来的？种子落地生根，西的也能长成东的。

root: 古英语 saed「被播撒之物」，与动词 sow（播种）同源，均出自重构的印欧词根 *sehi-「播撒」。起因义、种子选手义与动词义都从「埋进土里的一粒」展开。

sensesIntro.en: From one buried grain grow four directions: new plants, new ideas, new rankings, new fields.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一粒埋进土里的种子长出四个方向：新植物、新想法、新排名、新田地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one grain pressed into dark soil, holding a future
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒按进黑土的种子，装着未来

branches.en: the grain itself, inside fruit or packet
branches.cn: 颗粒本身，在果实或纸袋里

branches.en: a small cause that later fills a field
branches.cn: 日后占满一整片田的小小起因

branches.en: players planted in a fixed bracket
branches.cn: 被安置在固定对阵位置的选手

branches.en: the act of scattering grains by hand
branches.cn: 亲手播撒颗粒的动作

branches.en: grain, cause and sowing share one picture
branches.cn: 颗粒、起因与播种共享同一画面

intro.en: English words grown from the seed and sow family.
intro.cn: 由 seed 与 sow 词族长出的英语词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin cognates; seed is native Germanic, so the list stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: seed 为日耳曼本族词，无拉丁同源词，列表留空。

items.meaning: a grain that grows into a plant
items.example: Store the seeds in a cool place.
They met in a seedy bar.
items.exampleCN: 他们在一家破旧的酒吧见面。

items.meaning: the first funds to start a project
items.example: The lab was built with seed money.
items.exampleCN: 实验室靠启动资金建成。

items.example: The garden has gone to seed.
Seedless grapes are easier to eat.

items.meaningCN: 喂食——形近但词源不同，来自古英语 fedan
items.example: Please feed the cat at noon.

definition_zh: 以前；先前；此前；前面提到的
definition_en: at an earlier time, either before now or before a past moment that has already been mentioned
core_image: 行路人回头看向身后那条已经走过的路，路的尽头是旧日的景象
scene: 她翻看旧合同时才发现，这间屋子最早并不是办公室。 The room had previously been used as a storeroom.
sceneCN: 这里 previously 是「此前、在那之前」（第 2 个义项：在已经提到的某个过去时间点之前）；句意为这间屋子此前曾被用作储藏室。图中可辨识物件：摊开的旧合同、空荡的房间、墙角的纸箱。

pos.zh: （书面）前面提到的；先前所述的

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词词尾 -ly 即得形容词 previous，义为「以前的；先前的」
由 previous 加介词 to 构成的固定说法，用作介词，义为「在……之前」

senses.title: At a time before now
senses.definition: at some time in the past, seen from the point of view of the present
senses.definitionCN: 站在现在回看，事情发生在过去某个时候
senses.example: The shop was previously a bank.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店以前是一家银行。
senses.why: Latin praevius described what goes before on a road; time is pictured the same way, with earlier events lying further back along it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praevius 描述路上走在前面的东西；时间也被这样设想，更早的事就留在路更靠后的位置，所以「以前」是这个词最朴素的用法。

senses.title: Before a particular moment in the past
senses.definition: before an earlier point in time that is already being talked about
senses.definitionCN: 在已经提到的某个过去时间点之前
senses.example: She had previously worked in the same office for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 她此前在同一间办公室工作过十年。
senses.why: The same word can serve a second reference point; English marks the extra distance back with the past perfect instead of coining a new adverb.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也能为第二个参照点服务；英语用过去完成时来标示这多出来的一段距离，而不另造一个新副词。

senses.title: Mentioned earlier in a text
senses.titleCN: （书面）前面提到的；先前所述的
senses.definition: used to refer to something already stated earlier in a text or a discussion
senses.definitionCN: 用来指文章或谈话中已经说过的内容
senses.example: The previously described method works only on small samples.
senses.exampleCN: 前面描述的那种方法只适用于小样本。
senses.why: Writing puts words in a line, so what came before on the page is read as what came before in time; the adverb simply points backwards along that line.
senses.whyCN: 书写把词排成一行，纸面上先出现的内容就被读成时间上先出现的内容，这个副词只是沿着那一行往后指一指。

intro.en: Previously is an English ending added to previous, a word built in Latin from before plus way: the earlier thing is the one further back along the road.
intro.cn: previously 是在 previous 后面加英语副词词尾构成的，而 previous 在拉丁语里由「在前」与「路」组合而成：更早的事，就是留在路更后方的那一段。

items.en: Prae- meant before or in front, and here it marks what lies ahead on a road.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在……前面」，这里标示路上位于前面的东西。

items.en: Via meant way or road, and it is also the source of trivial, deviate and obviate.
items.cn: via 意为「路、道路」，trivial、deviate、obviate 也都出自它。

items.en: Praevious described someone or something going before, leading the way, or placed in front.
items.cn: praevius 形容走在前面、带路或位于前方的人或物。

items.en: English formed previous from that Latin adjective; it is first recorded in the seventeenth century, though the exact decade is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语用这个拉丁形容词造出 previous；一般认为它最早见于十七世纪，具体年代尚不确定。

items.en: Adding -ly makes an adverb, and the same ending turns a position on a road into a position in time.
items.cn: 加上 -ly 构成副词，同一个词尾把「在路上的位置」转成了「时间上的先后」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin word for road or the prefix meaning before; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs that point to an earlier time.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「路」的拉丁词或表示「在前」的前缀；近义组收指向更早时间的副词。

entries.definition: Coming or happening before the one mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 在提到的那一个之前的；先前的。

entries.definition: Allowing water or light to pass through; it uses the same road word with per-, through.
entries.definitionCN: 可让水或光透过的；它与 previous 共用表示「路」的词根，前缀 per- 意为「穿过」，只是拼写接近。

entries.definition: Not letting anything pass through, or not affected by something.
entries.definitionCN: 任何东西都透不过的；也指不受某事物影响。

entries.definition: The ability to see what will happen; its second element comes from a verb meaning to see, not from the word for road.
entries.definitionCN: 预见未来的能力；后半部分来自表示「看」的动词，而非表示「路」的词，与本词只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: In an earlier period, when things were different.
entries.definitionCN: 在早先某个时期，当时情况与现在不同。

entries.definition: At a time before the one being discussed.
entries.definitionCN: 在所讨论的时间之前。

entries.definition: At an earlier time, without naming the exact point.
entries.definitionCN: 在更早的时候，不点明具体时点。

entries.definition: Up to this time, used mostly in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 直到此时为止，多用于书面语。

entries.definition: At some time in the past, as in a once-famous singer.
entries.definitionCN: 在过去某个时候，如「曾经出名的歌手」。

normalIntro.en: The word is the Latin word for road with a prefix meaning before, plus an English ending that turns it into an adverb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「路」的词加上表示「在前」的前缀，再加一个英语副词词尾。

normal.en: Prae- plus via: previous is literally what is ahead on the road, and then what is earlier in time.
normal.cn: prae- 加 via：previous 字面上是「路上在前面的」，再转成时间上更早的。

normal.en: The same via gives deviate, to turn off the road, and obviate, to clear the road away.
normal.cn: 同一个 via 还给出 deviate（离开道路）与 obviate（把路清掉）。

normal.en: Previously is simply previous plus -ly, the ending that turns an adjective into an adverb of time or manner.
normal.cn: previously 就是 previous 加 -ly，这个词尾把形容词变成表示时间或方式的副词。

normal.en: Per- means through, so pervious describes something water can pass through; previous and pervious differ by one letter.
normal.cn: per- 意为「穿过」，所以 pervious 形容水能穿过的物体；previous 与 pervious 只差一个字母。

normal.en: In a paragraph, previously points back to what has already been said, which is the stretch of road already walked.
normal.cn: 在段落里，previously 指向已经说过的内容，也就是已经走过的那段路。

abstract.en: Time is treated as a road here: what is behind you is earlier, what is ahead is later.
abstract.cn: 这里把时间当成一条路：身后的更早，前面的更晚。

abstract.en: One letter separates previous from pervious, and one prefix separates going before from passing through.
abstract.cn: 一个字母隔开 previous 与 pervious，一个前缀隔开「走在前面」与「穿过去」。

abstract.en: Previously is what a writer says before adding: this was already true, and you may have forgotten it.
abstract.cn: previously 是作者在补充一句之前先说的：这件事早就成立，你可能已经忘了。

examples.en: The shop was previously a bank.
examples.cn: 这家店以前是一家银行。

examples.en: The room had previously been used as a storeroom.
examples.cn: 这间屋子此前曾被用作储藏室。

examples.en: As previously agreed, the meeting will start at nine.
examples.cn: 按照先前商定的，会议将在九点开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音近「普瑞维斯里」——previous 是「先前的」，尾巴再加一个里，就成了「先前里」，也就是以前。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ via（路）→ praevius（走在前面的）→ 英语 previous（先前的），再加副词词尾 -ly 得 previously。一般认为 previous 最早见于十七世纪，具体年代存疑。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being further back along the road; the senses split by their reference point, now or a past moment, and then by a text's earlier pages.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「在路上的更后方」；义项按参照点分开，或对着现在，或对着过去的某一刻，最后是文章里更靠前的段落。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller glancing back at the stretch of road already walked.
core.cn: 核心意象：行路人回头看向自己已经走过的那段路。

branches.en: an old sign still naming the shop's former business
branches.cn: 旧招牌上还写着店铺从前的营生

branches.en: a desk cleared before the new owner arrived
branches.cn: 新主人到来前就清空的桌子

branches.en: a line in a report pointing to a page above
branches.cn: 报告里指向前面某页的一行字

branches.en: a photograph taken long before the renovation
branches.cn: 装修很久之前拍的一张照片

branches.en: a footnote saying the point was already made
branches.cn: 脚注里说这一点前文已述

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix of place on the Latin noun for road, plus an English ending that turns the whole thing into an adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示位置的拉丁前缀加拉丁语「路」这个名词，再加一个把整体变成副词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: in the manner of, at the time of

latinEntries.meaningCN: 挡在路上的；迎面而来的

definition_zh: 重量；体重；重物；权重；砝码；分量
definition_en: how heavy a person or thing is, or the force with which a body is pulled toward the ground
core_image: 秤盘上沉甸甸压下的那一格刻度
scene: 体检报告出来那天，他盯着数字沉默了。 The doctor told him that his weight had increased by three kilograms.
sceneCN: 这里 weight 是「体重」（第 2 个义项：人或身体的重量）；句意是医生告诉他体重增加了三公斤。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「称重；权衡」，weight 由其历史尾音 -t 固化而来
weight + lifting 复合词，义为「举重」

senses.title: How heavy something is
senses.definition: the amount that a thing weighs, measured in units such as kilograms
senses.definitionCN: 物体有多重，以千克等为单位计量
senses.example: The bridge has a strict weight limit for trucks.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥对卡车有严格的限重。
senses.why: The most direct sense: heaviness as a number read off the scale.
senses.whyCN: 最直接的义项：重量就是从秤上读出的那个数字。

senses.title: Body weight
senses.definition: the heaviness of a person's body, often watched for health
senses.definitionCN: 人的身体重量，常与健康相关而受关注
senses.example: She has been trying to lose weight since spring.
senses.exampleCN: 她从春天起一直在努力减肥。
senses.why: The general measure of heaviness attaches to the most personal object we carry: our own body.
senses.whyCN: 一般意义的「多重」附着到我们随身携带的最切身之物上：自己的身体。

senses.title: A heavy object
senses.definition: a piece of metal or other heavy material used to hold things down or on scales
senses.definitionCN: 用来压住东西或放在秤上的金属或其他重物
senses.example: Use paper weights to stop the map blowing away.
senses.exampleCN: 用镇纸压住地图，免得被风吹走。
senses.why: What is heavy can itself be made into an object: the measure becomes the tool.
senses.whyCN: 「重」的东西本身可以做成一件器物：度量之物变成了工具。

senses.title: Importance or influence
senses.definition: the importance, influence, or authority of a person, argument, or fact
senses.definitionCN: 人、论据或事实的重要性、影响力或权威性
senses.example: His opinion carries a lot of weight in the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 他的意见在委员会里很有分量。
senses.why: Heavy things sink the balance, so importance is felt as literal heaviness on the scale of judgment.
senses.whyCN: 重的一端会让天平倾斜，于是在判断的天平上，重要性被感受为实实在在的沉重。

senses.title: The downward force of gravity
senses.titleCN: 重力；地心引力作用的力
senses.definition: in physics, the force by which a body is pulled toward the earth
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中物体被拉向地面的力
senses.example: In orbit, astronauts experience almost no weight.
senses.exampleCN: 在轨道上，宇航员几乎感受不到重力。
senses.why: The everyday pull on everything is formalized by science as a measurable force.
senses.whyCN: 日常压着万物的下拉感被科学形式化为可测量的力。

senses.title: A burden or worry
senses.definition: a heavy load, or a worry that presses on the mind
senses.definitionCN: 沉重的负荷，或压在心头的忧虑
senses.example: The debt was a weight on his shoulders for years.
senses.exampleCN: 那笔债多年来一直压在他的肩头。
senses.why: Physical heaviness extends to anything that drags a person down, inside or outside.
senses.whyCN: 身体的沉重延伸到一切拖累人的事物，无论身内身外。

senses.title: The heaviest or hardest part
senses.definition: the largest share or most demanding part of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事中占比最大或最费力的部分
senses.example: The weight of the work fell on the new team.
senses.exampleCN: 大部分工作落在了新团队身上。
senses.why: When a load is shared, the heaviest share is called the weight of it.
senses.whyCN: 当负担被分担时，最重的那一份就被称为整件事的「重量」。

senses.title: To add weight or bias to something
senses.definition: to make a statistic, system, or object heavier or biased toward one side
senses.definitionCN: 使统计、系统或物体更重，或偏向一方
senses.example: The final score is weighted toward the written exam.
senses.exampleCN: 最终成绩向笔试倾斜（加大权重）。
senses.why: Adding literal weight tips a balance; adding figurative weight tips a system toward one side.
senses.whyCN: 加上实重会让天平倾斜，加上比喻的「重」则让系统向一方倾斜。

intro.en: Weight grew out of the same Germanic carrying verb as weigh, fixed into a noun by an old ending.
intro.cn: weight 与 weigh 同出一个日耳曼语「搬运」动词，经一个古老词尾固定为名词。

items.en: The root *wegh- meant to move or transport, especially by wheeled vehicle.
items.cn: 词根 *wegh- 意为「移动、运送」，尤指用车载运。

items.en: The noun *wihtiz is generally reconstructed as that which is carried or drawn.
items.cn: 一般认为日耳曼名词 *wihtiz 指「被搬运、被拖拽之物（的重量）」。

items.en: Old English wiht meant weight or amount, paired with the verb wegan (to carry).
items.cn: 古英语 wiht 意为「重量、分量」，与动词 wegan（搬运）相配。

items.en: Middle English weight absorbed a -t by analogy with words like might and light, reshaping the spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语在类推 might、light 等词后添入 -t，形成今天的拼写 weight。

items.en: The figurative sense of importance and influence became common in political and legal writing.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪，「分量、影响力」的比喻义在政治与法律写作中普及。

items.en: Physics later fixed weight as the force of gravity on a mass, distinct from mass itself.
items.cn: 近代物理学将 weight 确立为质量所受的重力，与 mass 相区分。

note.en: Weight is twin to weigh in spelling history and is often mixed up with wait, which only shares the sound.
note.cn: weight 与 weigh 拼写史上是孪生词，又与只有读音相同的 wait 常被混淆。

entries.definition: to measure how heavy something is; to consider carefully
entries.definitionCN: 称重；权衡。weight 的同根动词，历史尾音 -t 区分二者

entries.definition: to stay until something happens
entries.definitionCN: 等待。与 weight 同音异源，只是拼写发音巧合相近

entries.definition: heavy or important
entries.definitionCN: 沉重的；重要的。weight 的形容词

entries.definition: adjusted so that one factor counts more
entries.definitionCN: 加权的；偏向一方的。常用于统计与评分

entries.definition: how tall or high something is
entries.definitionCN: 高度。与 weight 同属「-ight 计量名词」家族，词根无关

entries.definition: the amount of matter in a body
entries.definitionCN: 质量。物理学中与 weight（重力）严格区分

entries.definition: the quality of being heavy
entries.definitionCN: 沉重（的性质）。日常描述词，无计量含义

entries.definition: a heavy load or duty
entries.definitionCN: 重担；负担。对应 weight 的比喻负担义

entries.definition: the quality of mattering much
entries.definitionCN: 重要性。对应 weight 的「分量、影响力」比喻义

entries.definition: something heavy that is carried
entries.definitionCN: 负载；负荷。强调被搬运之物，不强调计量

normalIntro.en: Weight is easy to remember through weigh plus t and its -ight measuring family.
normalIntro.cn: 用 weigh 加 t 和 -ight 计量词家族来记 weight 很容易。

normal.en: weigh + t = weight: add the t to get the noun.
normal.cn: weigh 加 t 就是 weight：加上 t 得到名词。

normal.en: height, light, might, weight: the -ight family.
normal.cn: height、light、might、weight：-ight 词家族。

normal.en: put on weight, lose weight: the body goes up and down.
normal.cn: put on weight、lose weight：体重有升有降。

normal.en: carry weight: a heavy opinion that sinks the balance.
normal.cn: carry weight：有分量的意见，能让天平沉下去。

normal.en: pull one's weight: do your share of the heavy rowing.
normal.cn: pull one's weight：划桨时使出自己那份力气。

abstract.en: Picture a number on the bathroom scale refusing to move.
abstract.cn: 想象体重秤上的数字纹丝不动。

abstract.en: Feel a coin purse in each hand, one dragging the arm down.
abstract.cn: 两手各拎一个钱袋，一只手明显被拽得下沉。

abstract.en: See a courtroom balance tip when a famous expert speaks.
abstract.cn: 看法庭的天平在某位权威开口时倾斜。

examples.en: Check the weight of your luggage before the flight.
examples.cn: 登机前先称一下行李重量。

examples.en: Her advice carried real weight with the board.
examples.cn: 她的建议在董事会里很有分量。

examples.en: He lost weight by walking every evening.
examples.cn: 他靠每天晚上散步减了体重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂特」——食堂阿姨「喂」你的时候总给「特」别多，吃多了自然有「重量」。

root: weight 源自古英语 wiht「重量、分量」，与动词 wegan（今 weigh）同出原始日耳曼语 *wihtiz／*wegan，最终可追溯至原始印欧语词根 *wegh-「移动、运送」（同源词有 vehicle、wagon）。中古英语类推 might、light 等词而添入 -t。

sensesIntro.en: From the number on the scale, weight reaches body mass, metal measures, influence, gravity, burdens, shares of work, and statistical bias.
sensesIntro.cn: 从秤上的读数出发，weight 依次覆盖体重、金属重物、影响力、重力、精神负担、工作份额与统计权重。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale needle dropping under something heavy
core.cn: 核心意象：秤针被重物压落

branches.en: the measured number applies to things and to our body
branches.cn: 计量读数既用于物体也用于身体

branches.en: the measure becomes a metal tool that holds things down
branches.cn: 度量之物变成压住东西的金属器物

branches.en: science defines the pull of gravity itself
branches.cn: 科学把这种下拉定义为重力本身

branches.en: heaviness turns into burden and the heaviest share of work
branches.cn: 沉重化为负担与工作里最重的份额

branches.en: weight tips judgments and systems, becoming influence and bias
branches.cn: 重量让判断与系统倾斜，成为影响力与权重

intro.en: Weight has no living affixes of its own; its structure shows in the family built on weigh and -weight compounds.
intro.cn: weight 本身无活用词缀；其结构体现在 weigh 词族和 -weight 复合词中。

latinIntro.en: The Latin cousin vehere links weight's root to transport words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词 vehere 把 weight 的词根与「运送」词族相连。

items.meaning: the sport of lifting heavy bars
an object to hold papers down
a small thing added to complete a weight
items.meaningCN: 补足分量的小物；凑数之物

derivatives.zh: weight 派生，义为「重要的；沉重的」

definition_zh: 出价；投标；努力争取
definition_en: to offer a price, or to make an effort to get something
core_image: 拍卖师举起木槌等下一个价
scene: 拍卖师举起木槌，等着下一个价。 She bid twice for the old painting.
sceneCN: 这里 bid 是「出价」（第 1 个义项：在交易中报出愿付的价钱）；句意是她为那幅旧画出了两次价。

derivatives.zh: 由 bid 加 -der 构成，义为「出价者」
由 bid 加 -ding 构成，义为「竞标」
由 out- 加 bid 构成，义为「出价高于」
由 over- 加 bid 构成，义为「出价过高」

senses.title: To offer a price
senses.definition: to offer a sum of money for something
senses.definitionCN: 为某物报出愿付的价钱
senses.example: She bid twice for the old painting.
senses.exampleCN: 她为那幅旧画出了两次价。
senses.why: This is the commercial sense, heard at auctions and tenders.
senses.whyCN: 这是商业义，常见于拍卖与招标场合。

senses.title: To say farewell
senses.definition: to say goodbye or greet someone formally
senses.definitionCN: 正式道别或问候
senses.example: He bade farewell to his friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他向朋友们道别。
senses.why: The old sense was to announce or command, and farewell kept it.
senses.whyCN: 古义是「宣告、吩咐」，道别保留了这一层。

senses.title: To try to win something
senses.definition: to make an effort to gain something
senses.definitionCN: 为获得某物而努力
senses.example: The city will bid to host the games.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市将申办运动会。
senses.why: Offering a price turned into offering a plan or effort.
senses.whyCN: 报出价钱，引申为报出方案或努力。

intro.en: Bid comes from an Old English verb meaning to offer or command.
intro.cn: bid 来自一个意为「提供、吩咐」的古英语动词。

items.en: beodan meant to offer or announce.
items.cn: beodan 意为「提供、宣告」。

items.en: bidden meant to command or ask.
items.cn: bidden 意为「吩咐、请求」。

items.en: bid named a price at an auction.
items.cn: bid 指拍卖中的出价。

items.en: bid for contracts became common.
items.cn: 投标承接合同变得常见。

items.en: the past tense stays bid.
items.cn: 如今过去式仍是 bid。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group gives offer words.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组是表示报价的词。

entries.definition: large in size
entries.definitionCN: 大的

entries.definition: a small piece
entries.definitionCN: 一点

entries.definition: a young flower or leaf
entries.definitionCN: 花蕾

entries.definition: to say you will pay or give
entries.definitionCN: 提供；出价

entries.definition: to make a formal offer
entries.definitionCN: 投标

entries.definition: to put forward a plan
entries.definitionCN: 提议

normalIntro.en: Bid is the price you offer and the effort you offer.
normalIntro.cn: bid 既是你报出的价钱，也是你付出的努力。

normal.en: The past tense is bid, not bidded.
normal.cn: 过去式是 bid，不是 bidded。

normal.en: Bid for means offer money for.
normal.cn: bid for 指为……出价。

normal.en: The person is a bidder.
normal.cn: 出价的人叫 bidder。

normal.en: Outbid means offer more than others.
normal.cn: outbid 指出价高于别人。

normal.en: Bid farewell is a formal goodbye.

abstract.en: See an auctioneer holding a wooden hammer.
abstract.cn: 想象拍卖师握着木槌。

abstract.en: See a sealed envelope sent for a contract.

examples.en: She bid twice for the old painting.
examples.cn: 她为那幅旧画出了两次价。

examples.en: He bade farewell to his friends.
examples.cn: 他向朋友们道别。

examples.en: The city will bid to host the games.

sensesIntro.en: Offering money, offering a farewell and offering an effort share one old verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 报出价钱、道出告别、付出努力，共用一个古老动词。

branches.cn: 道别

definition_zh: 生产者；制造商；制片人；（生态）生产者
definition_en: a person or company that makes goods, or the one who organizes a film or programme
core_image: 车间尽头的一双手给成品贴上标签，标签上写着出自谁手
scene: 剧组杀青那天，制片人站在监视器旁核对最后一份预算表。 On the last day of shooting, the producer checked the final budget beside the monitor.
sceneCN: 剧组杀青那天，制片人站在监视器旁核对最后一份预算表；句中的 producer 指「负责组织并推进影视制作的人」（第 3 个义项：影视或戏剧的制片人）。图中可辨识物件：监视器、预算表、场记板、折叠椅；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 生产者；制造商；制片人；（生态）生产者

senses.title: A maker of goods
senses.definition: a person or firm that makes goods for sale
senses.definitionCN: 制造货物以供出售的人或企业
senses.example: The producer shipped the first batch on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 制造商周一发出了第一批货。
senses.why: Producer is the doer form of produce, so it simply names whoever brings the goods forth.
senses.whyCN: producer 是 produce 的施动者形式，因此直接指把货物造出来的一方。

senses.title: The supplying side of an economy
senses.definition: the side of a market that makes and offers goods, as opposed to buyers
senses.definitionCN: 市场中制造并提供货物的一方，与买方相对
senses.example: Producers absorbed most of the higher input cost.
senses.exampleCN: 生产者承担了大部分上涨的投入成本。
senses.why: Economics splits a market into makers and takers, and producer names one whole side.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把市场分成制造方与取用方，producer 指其中一整侧。

senses.title: The organizer of a film or play
senses.definition: the person who arranges funding, staff and schedule for a film, play or series
senses.definitionCN: 为电影、戏剧或剧集安排资金、人员与进度的人
senses.example: On the last day of shooting, the producer checked the final budget beside the monitor.
senses.exampleCN: 杀青那天，制片人在监视器旁核对最后一份预算表。
senses.why: A show must be brought into existence like a product, so the one who arranges it takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 一部戏也要像产品一样被造出来，因此安排它的人沿用同一称呼。

senses.title: The organizer of a music recording
senses.definition: the person who supervises the recording, mixing and shape of a music release
senses.definitionCN: 监督录音、混音与成品形态的人
senses.example: The producer reshaped the album around a single riff.
senses.exampleCN: 制作人围绕一段乐句重塑了整张专辑。
senses.why: Music uses the same word because a record is assembled from parts under one hand.
senses.whyCN: 音乐沿用这个词，因为一张唱片是在一双手的安排下由各部分拼成的。

senses.title: A farmer or grower
senses.definition: a person or farm that grows crops or raises animals for sale
senses.definitionCN: 种植作物或饲养动物以供出售的人或农场
senses.example: Local producers sell directly at the Saturday market.
senses.exampleCN: 本地农业生产者周六直接在集市上出售。
senses.why: Growing food is one form of bringing forth, so farms count as producers in ordinary speech.
senses.whyCN: 种出食物是「带出」的一种，因此农场在日常语言里也算生产者。

senses.title: An organism that makes its own food
senses.titleCN: 生态学中自养的生产者
senses.definition: in ecology, an organism such as a plant that makes food from sunlight or chemicals
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中靠阳光或化学能自制食物的生物，如植物
senses.example: Green plants are the producers at the base of the food web.
senses.exampleCN: 绿色植物是食物网底层的生产者。
senses.why: Ecology borrowed the economic word for organisms that create food rather than consume it.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用这个经济词，指制造食物而非消耗食物的生物。

senses.title: The organizer of a broadcast
senses.titleCN: 广播电视节目的制作负责人
senses.definition: the person responsible for putting a radio or television programme together
senses.definitionCN: 负责把广播或电视节目组织成形的人
senses.example: The producer cut the interview to fit the half-hour slot.
senses.exampleCN: 制片人把访谈剪到半小时内。
senses.why: A programme is assembled to a fixed length, and the one who assembles it is named as a maker.
senses.whyCN: 节目要按固定时长拼装，负责拼装的人便被称为制造者。

senses.title: Producer responsibility in policy
senses.titleCN: 环境政策中的生产者责任
senses.definition: the duty placed on manufacturers to take back or fund the disposal of their products
senses.definitionCN: 要求制造商回收或出资处理其产品的义务
senses.example: New rules extended producer responsibility to packaging.
senses.exampleCN: 新规把生产者责任扩展到包装。
senses.why: Policy makes the maker answerable for the whole life of the thing made.
senses.whyCN: 政策让制造者对成品的整个生命周期负责。

intro.en: Producer is the English agent noun of produce, formed with the suffix -er on a verb that comes from Latin producere 'to lead forward'. The film and music senses are nineteenth- and twentieth-century extensions.
intro.cn: producer 是 produce 的英语施动名词，在源自拉丁 producere「向前引出」的动词上加 -er 构成；影视与音乐义是十九、二十世纪的延伸。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead, draw'. Through producere it reaches produce, product and producer.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉」，经 producere 通向 produce、product 与 producer。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere gave producere, 'to lead forward, bring out'.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere 构成 producere，意为「向前引出、带出」。

items.en: English took the verb through French; the agent suffix -er, from Old English -ere and French -eur, was added to name the doer.
items.cn: 英语经法语吸收这个动词，再加施动后缀 -er（源自古英语 -ere 与法语 -eur）来指做这件事的人。

items.en: From the sixteenth century a producer was simply one who brings something forth, whether crops or goods.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，producer 只指带出某物的人，无论作物还是货物。

items.en: In the nineteenth century theatre and later film gave the word its managerial sense: the person who funds and organizes a show.
items.cn: 十九世纪的戏剧以及后来的电影赋予这个词管理义：出资并组织演出的人。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first use of the film sense is not precisely dated, and the year is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：影视义的最早用例没有确切年代，给出的年份只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words that are often swapped; group two holds near roles that are not producers.
note.cn: 第一组是同根且常被互换的词；第二组是并非 producer 的近义角色。

entries.definition: The action itself, or farm goods as a noun; it is what a producer does, not the doer.
entries.definitionCN: 动作本身，或作名词指农产品；是 producer 所做的事，不是做的人。

entries.definition: What is made; a producer makes products, but product never names the maker.
entries.definitionCN: 被造出来的东西；生产者制造产品，但 product 从不指制造者。

entries.definition: The activity or total output; it names the making, while producer names the one making.
entries.definitionCN: 活动或总产出；指制造，而 producer 指制造者。

entries.definition: The person who shapes the performances and shots; the producer handles money and organization.
entries.definitionCN: 负责表演与镜头形态的人；制片人管钱与组织。

entries.definition: A firm that makes goods in factories; narrower and more industrial than producer.
entries.definitionCN: 在工厂制造货物的企业；比 producer 更窄、更工业。

entries.definition: The everyday word for one who makes something; it lacks the economic and media senses.
entries.definitionCN: 指制造者的日常词；不含经济与影视义。

entries.definition: A person who grows crops, especially fruit; it is the farming half of producer.
entries.definitionCN: 种植作物的人，尤指水果；是 producer 中务农的那一半。

entries.definition: A firm that provides goods to buyers; it stresses delivery rather than creation.
entries.definitionCN: 向买方提供货物的企业；侧重交付而非创造。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the agent suffix, the same-root family and the fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：施动后缀、同根词族与固定搭配。

normal.en: Produce plus -er: the one who brings the goods forth.
normal.cn: produce 加 -er：把货物带出来的那一方。

normal.en: The family runs produce, producer, production, product, productive and productivity.
normal.cn: 同族词有 produce、producer、production、product、productive 与 productivity。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: film producer, music producer, producer price, agricultural producer.
normal.cn: 固定说法：电影制片人、音乐制作人、出厂价、农业生产者。

normal.en: The same root appears in conduct, introduce, reduce and educate.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 conduct、introduce、reduce 与 educate 中。

normal.en: Ecology keeps the word for plants that make their own food.
normal.cn: 生态学保留这个词，指能自制食物的植物。

abstract.en: Picture a hand stamping a finished box with a name.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在成品箱上盖下一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture a person holding the schedule and the budget at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人同时拿着进度表与预算表。

abstract.en: Picture a green leaf quietly making food for a whole food web.
abstract.cn: 想象一片绿叶默默为整张食物网制造食物。

examples.en: The producer delayed the release until the soundtrack was finished.
examples.cn: 制片人把发行推迟到配乐完成之后。

examples.en: Coffee producers in the highlands formed a cooperative.
examples.cn: 高地的咖啡生产者组建了合作社。

examples.en: New packaging rules make the producer pay for collection.
examples.cn: 新的包装规定让生产者承担回收费用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「produce（生产）+ r（人）」——把东西造出来的人，就是生产者与制片人

root: 英语 produce + 施动后缀 -er；produce 源自拉丁 producere「向前引出」= pro- + ducere「引导」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one maker: a firm, a whole supplying side, a film organizer, a music organizer, a farmer, a plant, a broadcast organizer and finally a policy duty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个制造者：企业、整个供给方、影视制片人、音乐制作人、农户、植物、节目制作负责人，最后是政策义务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand at the end of a line stamping a name on every finished item.
core.cn: 核心意象：流水线末端一只手在每件成品上盖下名字。

branches.en: MAKER AND ITS DUTIES: one firm, a whole market side, and the responsibility policy lays on them.
branches.cn: 制造者与其责任：一家企业、整个市场一侧，以及政策加在它们身上的责任。

branches.en: ORGANIZER: a film and a broadcast are both assembled by one person holding money and schedule.
branches.cn: 组织者：电影与广播节目，都由一个掌钱与掌进度的人拼装。

branches.en: RECORD: music borrows the same role for a release built from parts.
branches.cn: 唱片：音乐为一张拼装而成的作品借用同一角色。

branches.en: GROWER: a farm brings forth crops, which is production in the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 农户：农场带出作物，是最古老意义上的生产。

branches.en: AUTOTROPH: a plant makes its own food, so ecology calls it a producer.
branches.cn: 自养者：植物自制食物，生态学便称之为生产者。

intro.en: Producer is an English agent noun on a Latin verb of leading forward, so its ending and root can be read separately.
intro.cn: producer 是在「向前引出」的拉丁动词上加英语施动后缀构成，词尾与词根可分读。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere and producere supply the root; the -er ending came into English from both Old English and French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere 与 producere 提供词根；-er 词尾同时来自古英语与法语。

items.example: The prefix sends the making forward into a result.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把制造送向前，成为结果。

items.example: Farms produce most of the local food.
items.exampleCN: 农场生产大部分本地食物。

items.structure: agent suffix, Old English -ere and French -eur
items.example: The suffix turns the action into a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成人。

items.example: The producer signed off the budget.
The product reached shops in June.

items.exampleCN: 两家公司指派了一位联合制片人。

definition_zh: 现实的；逼真的；可行的
definition_en: seeing things as they actually are and acting accordingly; looking or sounding like real life; achievable in practice
core_image: 画布上的静物与桌边实物几乎分不清
scene: 画布上的静物光影细腻，几乎与桌边的实物难以分辨。 Her plan for the trip was realistic and cheap.
sceneCN: 这里 realistic 是「现实的」（第 1 个义项：看清实际、不空想）；句意为她的旅行计划现实而省钱。画面里可留意：细腻的光影、几乎分不清的实物与画。

derivatives.zh: un- 与 realistic 复合，指不切实际的

senses.title: Seeing things as they are
senses.definition: judging situations by what is actually true and possible rather than by wishful thinking
senses.definitionCN: 按实际真实与可能来判断情况，而非凭一厢情愿
senses.example: Her plan for the trip was realistic and cheap.
senses.exampleCN: 她的旅行计划现实而省钱。
senses.why: Realistic adds the suffix -istic to real, so it describes a mind that keeps its eye on what actually exists.
senses.whyCN: realistic 在 real 后加后缀 -istic，因此它描述始终盯着实际存在的现实的心智。

senses.title: Looking like real life
senses.definition: represented so faithfully that it looks or sounds like real life
senses.definitionCN: 表现得太忠实，以致看起来或听起来像真实生活
senses.example: The painting is so realistic that it fools the eye.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画太逼真了，骗过了眼睛。
senses.why: Art that copies what truly exists is called realistic, because its standard is the real thing outside the frame.
senses.whyCN: 摹写真实存在之物的艺术被称为 realistic，因为它的标准是画框之外的真实之物。

senses.title: Achievable
senses.definition: of a goal or expectation, possible to reach within real limits
senses.definitionCN: 指目标或期望在真实限度内可以达到
senses.example: The team set realistic goals for the first year.
senses.exampleCN: 团队为第一年设定了可行的目标。
senses.why: A goal shaped by what is actually possible rather than by desire alone is described as realistic.
senses.whyCN: 按实际可能而非单凭愿望设定的目标，被称为 realistic。

intro.en: Realistic is English real with the suffix -istic, a learned ending that came through Latin from Greek; it describes what follows the real.
intro.cn: realistic 是英语 real 加上后缀 -istic，这个词尾经拉丁语来自希腊语；它描述合乎真实之物。

items.en: Res meant a thing, and realis meant belonging to a thing, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: res 意为事物，realis 意为属于事物的，是整个词族的根。

items.en: English borrowed real to mark what exists rather than what is imagined.
items.cn: 英语借入 real，用来标记存在之物而非想象之物。

items.en: The ending -istic came through Latin from Greek -istikos and forms adjectives of tendency or style.
items.cn: 词尾 -istic 经拉丁语来自希腊语 -istikos，构成表示倾向或风格的形容词。

items.en: The word first described art that copies life, then spread to plans and judgments that accept real limits.
items.cn: 这个词先描述摹写生活的艺术，随后扩展到接受真实限度的计划与判断。

items.en: Modern English uses realistic for practical judgment, lifelike representation, and reachable goals.
items.cn: 现代英语用 realistic 指务实的判断、逼真的表现与可达成的目标。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers words for practical judgment and lifelike quality.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的词；近义组收表示务实判断与逼真品质的词。

entries.definition: Actually existing.
entries.definitionCN: 真实存在的。

entries.definition: The state of being real.
entries.definitionCN: 真实的状态。

entries.definition: To become aware of or make real.
entries.definitionCN: 意识到或使实现。

entries.definition: A style that shows life as it is.
entries.definitionCN: 如实表现生活的风格。

entries.definition: Concerned with doing rather than theory.
entries.definitionCN: 关涉实行而非理论的。

entries.definition: Looking like a living thing.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像活物的。

entries.definition: Based on good judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 基于良好判断的。

entries.definition: Possible to reach.
entries.definitionCN: 可以达成的。

normalIntro.en: The word applies real in three directions: a mind that faces facts, an image that copies life, and a goal that respects limits.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把 real 用在三个方向：面对事实的心智、摹写生活的影像，以及尊重限度的目标。

normal.en: Realistic is real plus -istic, so it describes whatever keeps close to the real.
normal.cn: realistic 是 real 加 -istic，描述贴近真实之物。

normal.en: A realistic plan accepts what time and money actually allow.
normal.cn: 现实的计划接受时间与金钱的实际限度。

normal.en: A realistic painting copies light and shape so well that the eye is fooled.
normal.cn: 逼真的画把光与形摹得极像，以致骗过眼睛。

normal.en: Be realistic about a job means not expecting more than it can give.
normal.cn: be realistic about a job 意为不对它期望过高。

normal.en: Unrealistic is its direct opposite, built with the negative prefix un-.
normal.cn: unrealistic 是它的直接反义词，由否定前缀 un- 构成。

abstract.en: To be realistic is to measure desire against possibility.
abstract.cn: 现实，就是用可能性来量愿望。

abstract.en: A realistic image is convincing because it obeys the same rules as the eye.
abstract.cn: 逼真的影像之所以可信，因为它遵守与眼睛相同的规则。

abstract.en: Realism is not pessimism; it is the refusal to subtract facts.
abstract.cn: 现实主义不是悲观，而是拒绝把事实减掉。

examples.en: Her plan for the trip was realistic and cheap.
examples.cn: 她的旅行计划现实而省钱。

examples.en: The painting is so realistic that it fools the eye.
examples.cn: 这幅画太逼真了，骗过了眼睛。

examples.en: The team set realistic goals for the first year.
examples.cn: 团队为第一年设定了可行的目标。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞丽斯提克」——画得像真的一样，计划也量力而行，记住 realistic 是现实的、逼真的。

root: 拉丁语 res（事物）→ realis → 英语 real + 后缀 -istic → realistic；同族有 realism、realist、unrealistic。

sensesIntro.en: The core is closeness to the real; the senses divide into practical judgment, lifelike representation, and achievable goals.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「贴近真实」；义项分为务实判断、逼真表现与可达成目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a still-life painting whose light and shadow almost cannot be told from the objects beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅静物画，光影几乎无法与桌边实物分辨。

branches.en: a plan that fits the budget
branches.cn: 贴合预算的计划

branches.en: a painted apple the eye tries to bite
branches.cn: 逼真得让眼睛想去咬的画中苹果

branches.en: a goal set where feet can reach
branches.cn: 设在脚能够到的目标

branches.en: facts accepted and goals kept reachable
branches.cn: 接受事实与保持目标可达

branches.en: an image true to life and a plan true to means
branches.cn: 忠于生活的影像与忠于财力的计划

intro.en: The word is a Latin root with a learned suffix, and its family spreads across art, thought and practice.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根加学术词尾，其词族分布在艺术、思想与实践之间。

latinIntro.en: Latin res, a thing, and realis, belonging to a thing, are the recorded sources of the root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 res（事物）与 realis（属于事物的）是这个词根有记录可考的来源。

items.meaning: a style showing life as it is

definition_zh: 关键的；危急的；批判的；挑剔的
definition_en: extremely important, very serious, or ready to judge faults
core_image: 医生站在病床前，盯着监护仪上跳动的数字
scene: 医生盯着监护仪，数字忽然往下掉。 The next few hours will be critical for the patient.
sceneCN: 这里 critical 指「危急的」（第 1 个义项：生死攸关、极其严重的）；句意是接下来几个小时对病人来说十分危急。

pos.zh: 关键的；危急的；批判的；挑剔的

senses.title: Extremely important
senses.definition: so important that the whole outcome depends on it
senses.definitionCN: 重要到整个结果都取决于它
senses.example: Timing is critical in this experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个实验里，时机非常关键。
senses.why: A single point can carry the weight of everything after it.
senses.whyCN: 一个点，就能扛起它之后全部事情的分量。

senses.title: Very serious
senses.definition: serious enough to threaten life or success
senses.definitionCN: 严重到威胁生命或成败
senses.example: He is in critical condition after the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 撞车之后他处于危急状态。
senses.why: The same word marks the point where a life may turn.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词，标记出生命可能转向的那一点。

senses.title: Ready to judge faults
senses.definition: examining something closely to find its faults or merits
senses.definitionCN: 仔细审视以找出缺点或优点
senses.example: She has a critical eye for small details.
senses.exampleCN: 她对细枝末节有一双挑剔的眼睛。
senses.why: To judge well is to separate the true from the false.
senses.whyCN: 要判断得好，就得把真的和假的分开。

intro.en: Critical comes from Greek kritikos, able to judge, through Latin criticus.
intro.cn: critical 源自希腊语 kritikos（善于判断的），经拉丁语 criticus 而来。

items.en: Krinein meant to separate and to judge.
items.cn: krinein 意为分开与判断。

items.en: Kritikos described a person able to judge.
items.cn: kritikos 形容有能力判断的人。

items.en: Criticus named the judge of a text.
items.cn: criticus 指评判文本的人。

items.en: Critical first meant given to judging.
items.cn: critical 最初意为「爱评判的」。

items.en: Medicine gave it the sense of a decisive moment.
items.cn: 医学给了它「决定性的时刻」这一义。

items.en: It now also means extremely important.
items.cn: 今天它也指极其重要。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the crit- stem, and the meaning group names other words for what decides an outcome.
note.cn: 形近组共享 crit- 词干，近义组列出其他表示决定成败的说法。

entries.definition: a person who judges works
entries.definitionCN: 评判作品的人

entries.definition: the act of judging faults
entries.definitionCN: 指出缺点的行为

entries.definition: a standard used to judge
entries.definitionCN: 用来评判的标准

entries.definition: so important that everything depends on it
entries.definitionCN: 重要到一切都取决于它

entries.definition: needed for life or for success
entries.definitionCN: 生命或成功所必需的

entries.definition: settling an outcome for good
entries.definitionCN: 一举定下结果的

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a monitor at night to a red pen on a page.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从夜里的一台监护仪，挪到纸页上的一支红笔。

normal.en: Critical means the scale is tipping right now.
normal.cn: critical 的意思是，天平正在此刻倾斜。

normal.en: One hour decides the whole week.
normal.cn: 一个小时，定下整整一周。

normal.en: A critical eye and a critical hour are the same word.
normal.cn: 挑剔的眼和危急的时刻，用的是同一个词。

normal.en: The nurse speaks softly because every sound counts.
normal.cn: 护士说话很轻，因为每个声响都算数。

normal.en: Judging well is also a matter of life and death.
normal.cn: 判断得好，同样关乎生死。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a screen falling fast.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上一条快速下坠的线。

abstract.en: Picture a clock with one hand left.
abstract.cn: 想象一只只剩一根指针的钟。

abstract.en: Picture a margin covered in red marks.
abstract.cn: 想象页边写满红笔标记。

examples.en: This is a critical moment for the team.
examples.cn: 这是团队的关键时刻。

examples.en: The driver is still in critical condition.
examples.cn: 司机仍处于危急状态。

examples.en: Students should learn critical thinking early.
examples.cn: 学生应尽早学会批判性思维。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 critical 记成天平正在倾斜的那一刻：一切都压在这一刻上，所以既关键又危急。

root: 源自希腊语 kritikos（善于判断的），再往上是 krinein（分开、判断）；本义是「做出评判的」，经医学用法生出「决定性的、危急的」之义。

sensesIntro.en: From what decides an outcome, to what threatens a life, to the eye that judges.
sensesIntro.cn: 从决定结果的一点，到威胁生命的状况，再到评判的那双眼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a monitor line falling in a quiet ward.
core.cn: 核心意象：安静病房里快速下坠的监护曲线。

branches.en: One factor outweighs all the others.
branches.cn: 一个因素压过了其余所有因素。

branches.en: The same point can threaten a life.
branches.cn: 同一个点，也能威胁一条生命。

branches.en: The judging eye separates good from bad.
branches.cn: 评判的眼睛把好与坏分开。

branches.en: Importance and danger meet at the same hour.
branches.cn: 重要与危险，在同一个时辰相遇。

branches.en: Criticism is a way of caring about quality.
branches.cn: 批评是关心质量的一种方式。

intro.en: Critical adds -al to the stem crit-, and from it grow critically and criticality.
intro.cn: critical 在词干 crit- 后加 -al，再由它长出 critically 与 criticality。

latinIntro.en: Greek krinein, to judge, passed through Latin criticus into the stem crit-.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 krinein（判断）经拉丁语 criticus 进入词干 crit-。

items.meaning: in a decisive or judging way
items.meaningCN: 以决定性或评判性的方式
items.example: She looked at the plan critically.
items.exampleCN: 她带着评判的眼光看这份计划。

items.meaningCN: 处于关键或临界的性质
items.exampleCN: 工程师测量了临界程度。

items.example: The critic sat in the back row.

items.exampleCN: 这番批评被坦然接受了。

items.example: Do not criticize without a reason.
The report was uncritical of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告对计划不加评判。

latinEntries.meaning: a judge of texts or works
latinEntries.example: Latin criticus named the learned judge.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 criticus 指博学的评判者。

definition_zh: 区别；卓越；荣誉
definition_en: a clear difference between two things, or a high level of quality that earns respect
core_image: 两枚几乎一样的印章，边上一处小小的刻痕分出高下
scene: 两枚印章摆在桌上，只有侧面一道细痕不同。 She makes a clear distinction between work and family.
sceneCN: 这里 distinction 指「区别」（第 1 个义项：把两样东西分开来看）；句意是她把工作和家庭分得很清楚。

collocations.phrase: a clear distinction between the two

senses.title: A line drawn between two things
senses.definition: a clear difference between two things or people
senses.definitionCN: 两样东西或两个人之间明确的差别
senses.example: There is a fine distinction between the two words.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个词之间有细微的区别。
senses.why: A line thin as a hair still keeps two rooms apart.
senses.whyCN: 一根头发丝那么细的线，也能隔开两个房间。

senses.title: High standing and honour
senses.definition: excellence that earns respect, or an honour given for it
senses.definitionCN: 赢得尊重的出众，或因出众而得的荣誉
senses.example: She won distinction as a young chemist.
senses.exampleCN: 她年轻时作为化学家就赢得了声誉。
senses.why: Work that stands above the rest is given a separate name.
senses.whyCN: 高出众人的成绩，会被单独给一个名分。

intro.en: Distinction comes from Latin distinctio, a dividing, from distinguere, to separate by marking.
intro.cn: distinction 来自拉丁语 distinctio（划分），源头是 distinguere（做记号分开）。

items.en: Stinguere meant to prick a mark into a surface.
items.cn: stinguere 指在表面刺出记号。

items.en: Distinguere set the marked things apart from the rest.
items.cn: distinguere 把做过记号的东西与其余分开。

items.en: Distinctio named the dividing line itself.
items.cn: distinctio 指的就是那条分界线。

items.en: English took it as the act of telling things apart.
items.cn: 英语借入时指把事物分辨开的行为。

items.en: The sense of personal excellence appeared.
items.cn: 后来出现了个人卓越这一层意思。

items.en: A prize, a tone and a fair argument can all show distinction.
items.cn: 今天奖赏、文风与公正的论证都能显出卓越。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the marking stem, while the meaning group offers difference and praise side by side.
note.cn: 形近组共享「做记号」的词干，近义组则把差别与赞誉并排放在一起。

entries.definition: clear and clearly separate
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而分明的

entries.definition: to see or show a difference
entries.definitionCN: 看出或说明差别

entries.definition: marking something as its own
entries.definitionCN: 显出自身特点的

entries.definition: the way things are not the same
entries.definitionCN: 事物不同的地方

entries.definition: a sharp difference set side by side
entries.definitionCN: 并置时显出的鲜明差别

entries.definition: very high quality
entries.definitionCN: 极高的品质

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a hairline mark and end with a prize given for standing above the rest.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一道头发丝细的记号线开始，落到因出众而得的一个奖。

normal.en: Dis- plus stinct: a mark is pricked, and a line appears.
normal.cn: dis 加 stinct，刺出一道记号，界线就出来了。

normal.en: The distinction between the two words is easy to miss.
normal.cn: 这两个词的区别很容易被忽略。

normal.en: She served with distinction in a hard trade.
normal.cn: 她在一个艰难的行业里做得很出色。

normal.en: A good teacher draws a distinction between error and laziness.
normal.cn: 好老师会区分出错和偷懒。

normal.en: The prize added another distinction to her name.
normal.cn: 这个奖又给她的名字添了一份荣誉。

abstract.en: Picture two seals on a desk with one tiny notch apart.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上一对印章，只差一道小刻痕。

abstract.en: Picture a hairline drawn across a page, still dividing it.
abstract.cn: 想象纸上一道发丝细的线，依然把页面分开。

abstract.en: Picture a medal placed beside an ordinary cup.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚奖章摆在一只普通杯子旁边。

examples.en: The distinction between the two senses is small but real.
examples.cn: 两个义项之间的区别很小，却真实存在。

examples.en: He served with distinction in the navy.

definition_zh: 网络；网状系统；人脉；广播网；联网
definition_en: an interconnected system of lines, people, or devices, or to connect things into such a system
core_image: 一张撒开的渔网：每个网结都连着别的网结
scene: 渔网摊在甲板上，一个个网结彼此相连，把每个部分都串成一片。 A fishing net lies spread across the deck, and its knots form a network that links every part to the next.
sceneCN: 这里 network 是「网状结构、网络」（第 1 个义项：由线或节点交织成的网）；句意：一张渔网摊在甲板上，网结连成一张网，把每一处都连到下一处。图中可辨识物件：渔网、网结、甲板、缆绳、渔船；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 网络；网状系统；人脉网；广播网

senses.title: A mesh of connected lines: netting
senses.titleCN: 连成一片的网线：网状织物
senses.definition: a structure of cords or threads crossed and knotted so that every part is linked to the rest
senses.definitionCN: 由绳线交叉打结而成的结构，每一处都与其他部分相连
senses.example: A torn network of netting lay across the harbour stones.
senses.exampleCN: 一张破了的网摊在港口的石头上。
senses.why: Network began in the 1550s as net plus work, literally a net-like fabric or structure. The picture is physical: knots joined by threads.
senses.whyCN: network 在 16 世纪 50 年代由 net 加 work 构成，字面是“网一样的织物或结构”。画面是实体的：网结被网线连起来。

senses.title: An interlocking transport system
senses.definition: a system of rivers, canals, roads, or railways that cross and connect at many points
senses.definitionCN: 河流、运河、道路或铁路在许多点上交叉相连的系统
senses.example: A network of canals linked the inland farms to the port.
senses.exampleCN: 一张运河网把内陆农场与港口连了起来。
senses.why: The 1839 sense 'any complex, interlocking system' was first used of rivers, canals and railways. The mesh becomes a map of routes.
senses.whyCN: 1839 年出现的“任何复杂交织的系统”一义，最初用于河流、运河与铁路。实体的网变成了一张路线图。

senses.title: A broadcasting system of many transmitters
senses.titleCN: 由多个发射台组成的广播网
senses.definition: a group of radio or television stations that share programmes and transmit them over a wide area
senses.definitionCN: 共享节目、向广大地区播送的广播电台或电视台群体
senses.example: The radio network broadcast the speech to forty stations.
senses.exampleCN: 这家广播网把演讲播送到四十家电台。
senses.why: From 1914 the word named a broadcasting system of multiple transmitters. Signals travel from node to node, so the mesh becomes a web of stations.
senses.whyCN: 从 1914 年起，这个词指由多个发射台组成的广播系统。信号从一个节点传到另一个节点，网于是变成了一张电台之网。

senses.title: An interconnected group of people
senses.definition: a group of people who are connected through work, family, or shared interests and can help one another
senses.definitionCN: 通过工作、家庭或共同兴趣相连、能互相帮助的一群人
senses.example: Her network of former classmates helped her find work.
senses.exampleCN: 她由老同学组成的人脉网帮她找到了工作。
senses.why: The 1934 sense came from psychology: people as nodes, relationships as threads. The mesh is now social rather than physical.
senses.whyCN: 1934 年的义项来自心理学术语：人是节点，关系是网线。此时网是社会性的，而非实体的。

senses.title: A computer network: machines that talk
senses.titleCN: 计算机网络：会互相通信的机器
senses.definition: a set of computers and devices connected so that they can exchange data
senses.definitionCN: 为交换数据而连接起来的一组计算机与设备
senses.example: The lab's computers share one network and one printer.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室的计算机共用一个网络和一台打印机。
senses.why: When computers became nodes, the old mesh needed no new shape: each machine is a knot, each cable a thread. The word kept its picture and changed its material.
senses.whyCN: 当计算机成为节点时，这张网不需要新形状：每台机器是一个结，每根线缆是一根网线。词保留了画面，只换了材料。

senses.title: A utility grid: power and telephone lines
senses.titleCN: 公用事业网：电力与电话线路
senses.definition: the connected system of cables, pipes, or lines that carries power, water, or telephone signals
senses.definitionCN: 输送电力、水或电话信号的互联电缆、管道或线路系统
senses.example: The power network failed during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨期间电网瘫痪了。
senses.why: A grid is a mesh laid over a region. Power lines join substations as knots join threads, so network names any utility system with that shape.
senses.whyCN: 电网是铺在一片区域上的网。电线把变电站连起来，正如网线把网结连起来，因此 network 可指任何具此形状的公用系统。

senses.title: To cover with a net
senses.definition: to cover an area or object with netting, usually for protection
senses.definitionCN: 用网覆盖一片区域或一个物体，通常是为了保护
senses.example: They networked the orchard to keep the birds off the fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用网罩住果园，防止鸟啄食果实。
senses.why: The verb appeared in 1887 with the plainest sense: to put a net over something. It turns the noun's object into an action.
senses.whyCN: 动词义于 1887 年出现，意思最直白：把网盖在某物上。它把名词所指的对象变成了一个动作。

senses.title: To broadcast across a network
senses.definition: to send a programme out through several linked stations at once
senses.definitionCN: 同时通过多家相连的电台或电视台播送节目
senses.example: The show was networked across the whole country.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节目通过广播网在全国播送。
senses.why: From 1940 the verb meant to distribute a programme through a network of transmitters. The broadcast travels along every thread of the mesh.
senses.whyCN: 从 1940 年起，动词指通过发射台网络分发节目。广播沿着这张网的每一根线传出去。

senses.title: To connect computers together
senses.definition: to link computers or devices so that they can share data
senses.definitionCN: 把计算机或设备连接起来，使它们能共享数据
senses.example: Engineers networked the two sites with fibre-optic cable.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用光纤把两个站点联网。
senses.why: The 1972 computing sense turns the noun into a task: you tie new knots into the existing mesh until the machines can reach one another.
senses.whyCN: 1972 年的计算机义把名词变成一个任务：你把新的结系进已有的网里，直到机器能彼此抵达。

senses.title: To build professional contacts
senses.definition: to meet and cultivate useful contacts, especially for work
senses.definitionCN: 结识并经营有用的人脉，尤指为工作目的
senses.example: She networks at every conference she attends.
senses.exampleCN: 她每参加一次会议就经营一次人脉。
senses.why: The 1982 sense applies the verb to people: each new acquaintance is a knot added to a personal mesh. Nothing physical remains but the shape.
senses.whyCN: 1982 年的义项把动词用在人身上：每位新认识的人都是加入个人之网的一个结。实体消失了，只剩形状。

intro.en: Network is a plain English compound of net and work, first recorded in the 1550s for net-like fabric. Its modern senses are a series of metaphors laid on that mesh: transport in 1839, broadcasting in 1914, people in 1934, and finally computers.
intro.cn: network 是 net 与 work 的朴素英语复合词，16 世纪 50 年代首次记录，指网一样的织物。它的现代义项是一层层叠加在这张网上的比喻：1839 年的交通、1914 年的广播、1934 年的人群，最后是计算机。

items.en: Net is Old English net 'net, snare', a word old enough to serve as a metaphor for a moral or mental trap.
items.cn: net 是古英语 net“网、罗网”，这个词古老到可以被用作道德或心理陷阱的比喻。

items.en: Network is first recorded in the 1550s as net plus work, meaning a net-like fabric or structure.
items.cn: network 于 16 世纪 50 年代首次记录，由 net 加 work 构成，指网一样的织物或结构。

items.en: The sense 'any complex, interlocking system' appears in 1839, first applied to networks of rivers, canals and railways.
items.cn: “任何复杂交织的系统”一义出现于 1839 年，最初用于河流、运河与铁路的网络。

items.en: A network becomes a broadcasting system of multiple transmitters in 1914.
items.cn: 1914 年，network 开始指由多个发射台组成的广播系统。

items.en: The sense 'interconnected group of people' appears in 1934 as psychological jargon.
items.cn: “彼此相连的人群”一义于 1934 年出现，原为心理学术语。

items.en: The verb follows: to cover with a net in 1887, to broadcast in 1940, to link computers in 1972, and to build contacts in 1982.
items.cn: 动词随后跟进：1887 年“用网覆盖”，1940 年“通过广播网播送”，1972 年“计算机联网”，1982 年“建立人脉”。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, including a phrase that sounds like network; the second group is chosen for the mesh image they share.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写与读音挑选，其中有一个听起来像 network 的短语；第二组按它们共享的网状意象挑选。

entries.definition: the total value of assets minus liabilities. The phrase sounds almost like network but belongs to finance, not to nets.
entries.definitionCN: 资产总值减去负债。这个短语听起来几乎和 network 一样，但属于财务，与网无关。

entries.definition: a small, low-cost laptop of the late 2000s. It joins net to book, not to work.
entries.definitionCN: 21 世纪末流行的小型低价笔记本电脑。它把 net 与 book 组合，而不是与 work 组合。

entries.definition: material made of net or mesh. It is the noun from net, not a form of network.
entries.definitionCN: 网材；网。它是 net 派生的名词，不是 network 的变形。

entries.definition: a mesh spun by a spider, or any complex system of linked parts. It stresses threads woven by a maker, while network stresses nodes joined together.
entries.definitionCN: 蜘蛛结的网，或任何由相连部分构成的复杂系统。它强调由造物者织出的线，而 network 强调节点之间的连接。

entries.definition: a pattern of crossing lines, especially for power or streets. It is regular and geometric, while a network can grow irregularly.
entries.definitionCN: 交叉线构成的格网，尤指电网或街道网。它是规则、几何的，而 network 可以不规则地生长。

entries.definition: a material of connected strands with open spaces between them. It names the fabric itself rather than the system it forms.
entries.definitionCN: 由相连线股构成、中间有空隙的材料。它指织物本身，而不是织物形成的系统。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: net plus work in 1550s, then the dated extensions to transport, broadcasting, people and computers.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：16 世纪 50 年代的 net 加 work，随后是有年代可查的扩展——交通、广播、人群与计算机。

normal.en: net plus work says the whole thing plainly: work made of net, a net-like fabric.
normal.cn: net 加 work 说得很直白：用网做成的制成品，即网一样的织物。

normal.en: In 1839 the mesh became a map: rivers, canals and railways crossing at many points.
normal.cn: 1839 年，这张网变成了一张地图：河流、运河与铁路在许多点上交叉。

normal.en: In 1914 the mesh became stations: many transmitters sharing one broadcast.
normal.cn: 1914 年，这张网变成了电台：多个发射台共享一次广播。

normal.en: In 1934 people became the nodes, and in 1972 computers did: the shape stayed, the material changed.
normal.cn: 1934 年人成了节点，1972 年计算机成了节点：形状没变，材料变了。

normal.en: The verbs follow the nouns: cover with a net, broadcast, connect, and build contacts.
normal.cn: 动词跟随名词：用网覆盖、播送、联网、建立人脉。

abstract.en: Picture one knot with four threads leaving it: remove the threads and it is only a knot; the connections are what make it a network.
abstract.cn: 想象一个网结向四面伸出四根线：抽掉线，它只是个结；正是连接使它成为网络。

abstract.en: The same drawing works for a map, a radio system, a group of friends, and a room of servers.
abstract.cn: 同一幅图可以画成地图、广播系统、朋友圈，也可以画成一屋子的服务器。

abstract.en: Cut one thread and the mesh still holds: a network is judged by how many routes remain, not by any single knot.
abstract.cn: 剪断一根线，网仍然撑得住：网络的价值在于还剩多少条通路，而不在任何一个结。

examples.en: A dense network of trails connects the villages along the valley.
examples.cn: 一张密集的小路网连接着山谷里的村庄。

examples.en: The company rebuilt its computer network after the outage.
examples.cn: 停电事故后，公司重建了计算机网络。

examples.en: He spent the conference networking with editors and researchers.
examples.cn: 他在会议上忙着与编辑和研究人员建立人脉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内特网」——内里特别多网结，四面八方都连着 → network 网络、人脉

root: 由古英语 net“网、罗网”加 work“工作、制成品”复合而成，1550s 首次记录，核心是“网一样的连结结构”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of network all keep one shape: knots joined by threads. The material changes from cord to canals, transmitters, people, cables and computers, and the verb senses simply put the mesh into action.
sensesIntro.cn: network 的十个义项都保留同一个形状：网结被网线连起来。材料从绳索换成运河、发射台、人、电缆与计算机，动词义只是让这张网动起来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fishing net spread out, every knot tied to others.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张摊开的渔网，每个网结都连着别的结。

branches.en: FROM FABRIC TO MAP: literal netting, then a system of rivers, canals and railways.
branches.cn: 从织物到地图：字面的网，然后是河流、运河与铁路构成的系统。

branches.en: FROM STATIONS TO PEOPLE: transmitters sharing programmes, then people sharing contacts.
branches.cn: 从电台到人：共享节目的发射台，然后是共享关系的人。

branches.en: TECHNICAL GRIDS: computers exchanging data, and utility lines carrying power or signals.
branches.cn: 技术性网络：交换数据的计算机，以及输送电力或信号的公用线路。

branches.en: THE OLD VERBS: covering with netting, and sending a programme through many stations.
branches.cn: 较早的动词：用网覆盖，以及通过多家电台播送节目。

branches.en: THE MODERN VERBS: linking machines, and cultivating a personal web of contacts.
branches.cn: 现代动词：连接机器，以及经营个人的关系网。

intro.en: Network is the compound net plus work, with no Latin suffix. English adds -ing, -ed, -er and -able to it, and the same net appears in internet, intranet, netting and netbook.
intro.cn: network 是 net 加 work 的复合词，不含拉丁后缀。英语在它上面加 -ing、-ed、-er、-able，而同一个 net 也出现在 internet、intranet、netting、netbook 中。

latinIntro.en: Network is Germanic, not Latin. The Latin entries below are its nearest counterparts, given for contrast: rete 'net', nexus 'a binding', and nectere 'to bind'.
latinIntro.cn: network 属日耳曼语，不属拉丁语。下面列出的拉丁词是它最接近的对应词，仅供对照：rete“网”、nexus“联结”、nectere“捆缚”。

items.meaning: a mesh-like structure or connected system
items.meaningCN: 网状结构；相连的系统（net“网”+ work“制成品”）
items.example: The city's tram network covers the whole centre.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市的有轨电车网络覆盖了整个市中心。

items.meaning: the act of linking systems or building contacts
items.meaningCN: 联网；建立人脉（-ing 构成动名词）
items.example: Networking is half of the value of a conference.
items.exampleCN: 建立人脉是一场会议一半的价值。

items.meaningCN: 联网的；连成网的（-ed 构成形容词）

items.meaning: a person skilled at building contacts
items.meaningCN: 善于建立人脉的人（-er 构成人称名词）
items.example: She is the best networker in the sales team.
items.exampleCN: 她是销售团队里最会经营人脉的人。

items.meaning: a mesh of cord used to catch things
items.meaningCN: 网；罗网（network 的第一成分）
items.example: The fishermen repaired the net before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 渔民在黎明前修补了渔网。

items.meaningCN: 网材；网（-ing 构成材料名词）
items.example: Netting protected the young trees from deer.
items.exampleCN: 网罩保护了小树不被鹿啃食。

items.meaningCN: 互联网（inter-“在……之间”+ net“网络”）
items.example: The files were sent over the internet.

items.meaning: a private network inside an organisation
items.meaningCN: 内联网（intra-“在内部”+ net“网络”）
items.example: Staff read the policy on the company intranet.
items.exampleCN: 员工在公司内联网上读到这项政策。

items.meaning: a small laptop designed mainly for online use
items.meaningCN: 上网本（net“网络”+ book，指主要用于上网的小电脑）
items.example: He carried a netbook instead of a full laptop.
items.exampleCN: 他带了一台上网本，而不是完整的笔记本电脑。

items.meaning: capable of being connected to a network
items.meaningCN: 可联网的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: The printer is networkable and shared by the office.
items.exampleCN: 这台打印机可联网，供全办公室共用。

latinEntries.meaning: a net, a network of cords

latinEntries.meaningCN: 联结；联系（来自 nectere“捆缚”）

definition_zh: 有点；稍微；在某种程度上
definition_en: to a small degree, a little
core_image: 温度计的水银柱只升了一小格
scene: 下午天气有点凉。 The weather is somewhat cool in the afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 somewhat 是「有点；稍微」（第 1 个义项）；句意：下午天气有点凉。

senses.title: A little
senses.definition: to a small degree
senses.definitionCN: 达到较小的程度
senses.example: The weather is somewhat cool in the afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 下午天气有点凉。
senses.why: Some plus what marks an amount too small to name.
senses.whyCN: some 加 what，标出小到不必说出的程度。

senses.title: To some extent
senses.definition: partly, in some respects
senses.definitionCN: 部分地，在某些方面
senses.example: The two plans are somewhat similar.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个计划在某种程度上相似。
senses.why: A small degree becomes a stated part of the whole.
senses.whyCN: 微小的程度变成了整体中被说明的一部分。

intro.en: Somewhat joins some with the old pronoun what.
intro.cn: somewhat 把 some 与古老代词 what 组合在一起。

items.en: Sum meant some; hwæt meant what.
items.cn: sum 意为一些，hwæt 意为什么。

items.en: The compound named an unspecified amount.
items.cn: 这个复合词指未说明的数量。

items.en: It narrowed to mean a small degree.
items.cn: 它的含义缩小为较小的程度。

items.en: It became a common adverb before adjectives.
items.cn: 它成为常放在形容词前的副词。

items.en: The phrase somewhat of a added a noun use.
items.cn: somewhat of a 这一说法增加了名词用法。

note.en: Somewhat is compared with look-alike words and adverbs of small degree.
note.cn: 把 somewhat 与形近词以及表示小程度的副词作比较。

entries.definition: in some way
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式

entries.definition: in some place
entries.definitionCN: 在某处

entries.definition: on some occasions
entries.definitionCN: 有时

entries.definition: a little

entries.definition: to a certain degree
entries.definitionCN: 相当；有点

entries.definition: to a moderate degree
entries.definitionCN: 相当；还算

normalIntro.en: Somewhat turns the dial only a little.
normalIntro.cn: somewhat 只把刻度盘拧动一点点。

normal.en: The weather is somewhat cool in the afternoon.

normal.en: The two plans are somewhat similar.

normal.en: He was somewhat surprised by the news.

normal.en: The task is somewhat difficult.

normal.en: She is somewhat of an expert.
normal.cn: 她算得上半个专家。

abstract.en: Somewhat is the adverb of the half-open door.
abstract.cn: somewhat 是「半开的门」的副词。

abstract.en: Small degrees are still degrees.
abstract.cn: 小的程度仍然是程度。

abstract.en: What is somewhat true is not yet false.
abstract.cn: 有点真实的东西，还不算虚假。

examples.en: The weather is somewhat cool in the afternoon.

examples.en: The two plans are somewhat similar.
examples.cn: 这两个计划在某种程度上相似。

examples.en: He was somewhat surprised by the news.
examples.cn: 他对这个消息有点惊讶。

dict_mnemonic.text: somewhat 就是 some（某个）加 what（多少）：某个说不太清的小程度，就是「有点」；somewhat different 是「有些不同」，somewhat of a 是「有点像个」。

root: 由 some（某个）与 what（什么、多少）组合而成，核心义「某种小小的程度」。

sensesIntro.en: Somewhat means a little, or to some extent.
sensesIntro.cn: somewhat 意为有点，或在某种程度上。

core.en: A small, unnamed degree.
core.cn: 一个未说明的小小程度。

branches.en: The air holds a faint chill.
branches.cn: 空气里有一丝凉意。

branches.en: Two plans share some features.
branches.cn: 两个计划有部分共同点。

branches.en: A small degree is a partial truth.
branches.cn: 小小的程度，也是一种部分成立。

branches.en: Somewhat sits between very and not at all.
branches.cn: somewhat 坐在 very 与「一点也不」之间。

branches.en: To some extent is to a small measured extent.
branches.cn: 「在某种程度上」就是在一个小小的、可量度的程度上。

intro.en: Somewhat belongs to the some- family of degree and manner.
intro.cn: somewhat 属于由 some 构成、表示程度与方式的词族。

latinIntro.en: Somewhat has no Latin root; both parts are Old English.
latinIntro.cn: somewhat 没有拉丁词根，两部分都来自古英语。
