definition_zh: 非凡的；值得注意的；惊人的；值得称道的
definition_en: unusual in a way that is worth noticing, often in a good sense
core_image: 一群普通房子中间忽然立起一座通体发亮的塔
scene: 那支球队从垫底一路打进决赛，整个城市都在谈论这件事。 The team climbed from last place to the final, a remarkable run that the whole city talked about.
sceneCN: 这里 remarkable 是「非凡的」（第 1 个义项：不同寻常且值得注意）；句意：这支球队从最后一名一路打进决赛，这段非凡的历程被全城谈论。

pos.zh: 非凡的；值得注意的；惊人的；值得称道的

derivatives.zh: remarkable 加 -ly 构成，义为「非凡地；出乎意料地」
remarkable 的动词来源，义为「评论；注意到」
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「平淡无奇的」

senses.title: Unusual and worth noticing
senses.definition: unusual enough to attract attention and deserve comment
senses.definitionCN: 不同寻常到足以引起注意并值得一说
senses.example: The bridge is a remarkable piece of engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是一项非凡的工程。
senses.why: Remarkable is literally what can be remarked on, so anything that draws comment is remarkable.
senses.whyCN: remarkable 字面上是「可以被谈论的」，因此任何引人评论的事物都称得上非凡。

senses.title: Surprising in degree
senses.definition: surprising because it is much greater or smaller than expected
senses.definitionCN: 因为比预期大得多或小得多而令人惊讶
senses.example: There is a remarkable similarity between the two paintings.
senses.exampleCN: 这两幅画之间有惊人的相似。
senses.why: When the amount of something passes expectation, it forces a remark, which is the surprise sense.
senses.whyCN: 当某事物的程度超出预期，人就会忍不住开口评论，这就是「惊人」这一义项。

senses.title: Deserving praise
senses.definition: so good that people admire it and talk about it with approval
senses.definitionCN: 好到让人钦佩并带着赞许谈论
senses.example: She made a remarkable recovery after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术之后她的恢复情况非常了不起。
senses.why: The same notice turns into praise when the thing noticed is good rather than merely strange.
senses.whyCN: 当被注意到的东西不只是奇特而且是好的，同一份注意就转为赞许。

intro.en: Remarkable is an English adjective built from the verb remark with the ending -able.
intro.cn: remarkable 是英语中由动词 remark 加词尾 -able 构成的形容词。

items.en: The verb remarquer, to mark or notice, supplies the base of the word.
items.cn: 古法语动词 remarquer「标记、注意」提供了这个词的基础。

items.en: Remark enters English, and -able is soon added to form an adjective.
items.cn: remark 进入英语后不久就加上 -able 构成形容词。

items.en: Remarkable first means worthy of being noted or commented on.
items.cn: remarkable 最初意为「值得被记下或谈论的」。

items.en: The word widens to mean excellent or extraordinary, especially in praise.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，词义扩展到「卓越的、非凡的」，多用于称赞。

items.en: Modern usage often prefers it for surprising facts and impressive achievements.
items.cn: 现代用法常用它形容令人惊讶的事实与令人印象深刻的成就。

note.en: Remarkable is the adjective of remark, and it stands beside words for extraordinary and impressive.
note.cn: remarkable 是 remark 的形容词，与表示非凡与令人印象深刻的词相邻。

entries.definition: in a way that is surprising or unusual
entries.definitionCN: 非凡地；出乎意料地，由 remarkable 加 -ly 构成

entries.definition: ordinary and not worth noticing
entries.definitionCN: 平淡无奇的，由否定前缀 un- 构成

entries.definition: to comment or notice
entries.definitionCN: 评论；注意到，是 remarkable 的动词来源

entries.definition: very unusual and impressive
entries.definitionCN: 非凡的；特别的，语气比 remarkable 更强

entries.definition: important enough to be noticed
entries.definitionCN: 显著的；值得注意的，偏正式

entries.definition: very noticeable because of being unusual
entries.definitionCN: 引人注目的，强调视觉或印象上的冲击

normalIntro.en: Remarkable means worth remarking on, so the whole word rests on the verb remark.
normalIntro.cn: remarkable 意为「值得被谈论的」，整个词都依托于动词 remark。

normal.en: Add -able to remark and you get the quality of deserving comment.
normal.cn: 在 remark 后加 -able，就得到「值得被评论」这种性质。

normal.en: Change the ending to -ably for the adverb remarkably.
normal.cn: 把词尾换成 -ably 就得到副词 remarkably。

normal.en: Put un- in front and the word means nothing worth noticing.
normal.cn: 在前面加 un-，这个词就表示「没有值得注意之处」。

normal.en: Remarkable progress and a remarkable achievement are the two most common pairings.
normal.cn: remarkable progress 与 a remarkable achievement 是最常见的两个搭配。

normal.en: The word often points to praise, not just surprise.
normal.cn: 这个词常带有赞许，而不只是惊讶。

abstract.en: Picture one lit tower among rows of ordinary houses.
abstract.cn: 想象一排普通房屋中忽然立起一座发亮的塔。

abstract.en: See a crowd turning its head at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象人群在同一瞬间转过头去。

abstract.en: Think of a record time that makes the announcer pause.
abstract.cn: 想一个让解说员停顿的记录成绩。

examples.en: The patient made a remarkable recovery.
examples.cn: 这位病人恢复得非常好。

examples.en: It is remarkable how quickly the children learned.
examples.cn: 孩子们学得这么快，实在令人惊讶。

examples.en: The two brothers share a remarkable resemblance.
examples.cn: 这两兄弟长得惊人地相像。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞马克伯」——想象一位叫马克伯的人在瑞丽做出惊人之举；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 由动词 remark（评论；注意到）加形容词词尾 -able 构成，词根可追至法语 marquer「做记号」。

sensesIntro.en: Anything worth remarking on can be remarkable, whether it is merely strange, surprisingly large, or genuinely excellent.
sensesIntro.cn: 任何值得一说的东西都可以叫 remarkable，无论它只是奇特、出人意料地大，还是确实优秀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lit tower standing among ordinary houses.
core.cn: 核心意象：普通房屋之间立着一座发亮的塔。

branches.en: What draws a mark draws attention, which is the core adjective sense.
branches.cn: 能留下标记的东西自然引人注意，这是核心形容词义。

branches.en: A degree far beyond expectation forces a comment of surprise.
branches.cn: 远超预期的程度会逼出一句惊讶的评论。

branches.en: When the noticed thing is good, notice becomes praise.
branches.cn: 当被注意到的事物是好的，注意就变成赞许。

branches.en: Both rest on the same act of mental marking.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在同一个心里做标记的动作上。

branches.en: Surprise and admiration are the two common colours of the word.
branches.cn: 惊讶与钦佩是这个词最常见的两种色彩。

intro.en: Remarkable stacks an English adjective ending onto a French verb borrowed into English.
intro.cn: remarkable 在借入英语的法语动词上叠加了一个英语形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The -able ending comes from Latin -abilis, meaning able to be, and the base is the marking root.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾 -able 来自拉丁语 -abilis，意为「能够被……的」，其基础是表示标记的词根。

items.example: Re- intensifies the marking in remark.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 加强了 remark 中「标记」的动作。

items.example: The mark root is shared with marker and landmark.
items.exampleCN: mark 词根与 marker、landmark 共用。
remarkable 意为「值得被谈论的」。

items.example: Remarkably turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: remarkably 把形容词变成副词。
unremarkable 表示「不值得注意的」。

items.example: Marquer supplies the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: marquer 提供了这一词族的基础。

items.meaning: a tool or sign that marks
items.example: Marker pairs the mark root with an agent ending.
items.exampleCN: marker 把 mark 词根与施事词尾组合在一起。

items.meaning: a feature that marks a place
items.example: Landmark keeps the boundary sense of the old root.
items.exampleCN: landmark 保留了古老词根的「边界」意味。

definition_zh: 难以置信地；极其；非常
definition_en: in a way that is very hard to believe, or used to mean extremely
core_image: 一句话说完，听者愣住，时间停了一拍
scene: 听完他说自己一口气跑完马拉松，你半天说不出话。 He ran incredibly fast and won the race with ease.
sceneCN: 这里 incredibly 是「极其、非常」（第 3 个义项：程度副词用法）；句意是他跑得快得惊人，轻松赢下比赛。

pos.zh: 副词：难以置信地；极其；非常

derivatives.zh: 义为「难以置信的」，是本词的基础形容词，去掉 -ly 即成
义为「可信的」，与本词同根，仅差否定前缀
义为「信用、信任」，与本词同含 cred- 词根
义为「可信度」，cred- 词根加名词后缀

senses.title: In a way that is hard to believe
senses.titleCN: 难以置信地：以令人难信的方式
senses.definition: in a manner that is so unusual that people find it hard to believe
senses.definitionCN: 以极其反常、让人难以相信的方式
senses.example: The story ends incredibly, with the hero walking out of the sea alive.
senses.exampleCN: 故事的结局令人难以置信：主人公活着从海里走了出来。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the plain sense of the adjective: an event resists belief, and the word says so.
senses.whyCN: 副词保留了形容词的本义：事件抗拒被相信，这个词就直接说出这一点。

senses.title: To a shocking degree of size or amount
senses.titleCN: 惊人到某种规模或数量
senses.definition: used to say that a size, amount, or degree is far beyond what is normal
senses.definitionCN: 表示规模、数量或程度远超寻常
senses.example: The bill was incredibly high after the long phone calls.
senses.exampleCN: 打了那么久的电话后，账单高得吓人。
senses.why: When a quantity passes belief, the word shifts from judging truth to measuring magnitude.
senses.whyCN: 当数量超出相信的范围，这个词就从判断真伪转向衡量大小。

senses.title: Extremely, as an intensifier
senses.titleCN: 极其：程度副词的加强用法
senses.definition: used before an adjective or adverb simply to mean very or extremely
senses.definitionCN: 用在形容词或副词前，只表示「非常、极其」
senses.example: She is incredibly kind to strangers who ask for help.
senses.exampleCN: 她对前来求助的陌生人极为友善。
senses.why: Daily speech wears the surprise down: what once defied belief now only adds emphasis.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语把惊异磨平了：曾经表示难以相信，如今只是加强语气。

senses.title: Used of behaviour that is hard to accept
senses.definition: used to describe conduct that seems shockingly careless or unfair
senses.definitionCN: 形容行为粗心或不公到令人震惊
senses.example: They acted incredibly badly by ignoring the complaint for months.
senses.exampleCN: 他们几个月不理投诉，表现得差劲得让人难以接受。
senses.why: The negative prefix also carries moral weight: such conduct should not be believed of anyone.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀也带道德分量：这种行为不该被相信会出自任何人。

intro.en: Incredibly is the adverb of incredible, from Latin in-, not, and credere, to believe, plus -bilis and the English -ly.
intro.cn: incredibly 是 incredible 的副词形式，源自拉丁语 in-（不）与 credere（相信），加 -bilis，再接英语 -ly。

items.en: Credere meant to trust or entrust, the same root behind credit and creed.
items.cn: credere 意为「信任、托付」，与 credit、creed 同根。

items.en: Incredibilis named what could not be believed, often of marvels and strange tales.
items.cn: incredibilis 指令人无法相信之事，常用于奇闻异事。

items.en: English borrowed incredible through French for tales that defied belief.
items.cn: 英语经由法语借入 incredible，用于不合常理的故事。

items.en: The adverb incredibly appeared, keeping the sense of in a manner hard to believe.
items.cn: 副词 incredibly 出现，保留「以难以相信的方式」之义。

items.en: The sense widened from judging truth to measuring size and degree.
items.cn: 词义从判断真伪扩展到衡量大小与程度。

items.en: Spoken English made it a plain intensifier meaning extremely.
items.cn: 英语口语把它变成普通的程度副词，义为「极其」。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cred- believe root; the near-meaning group holds adverbs of extreme degree.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示「相信」的 cred- 词根；近义组收表示极端程度的副词。

entries.definition: Too strange or extreme to be believed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以置信的」，是本词的基础形式。

entries.definition: Able to be believed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可信的」，与本词只差否定前缀与词尾。

entries.definition: The quality of not being believable.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不可信性」，同根的抽象名词，较罕见。

entries.definition: In a way that is impossible to believe.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「难以置信地」，与 unbelievable 对应，更口语。

entries.definition: To a very high degree, without any surprise.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「极其」，只表程度，不带惊异色彩。

entries.definition: In a way that stuns the observer.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「惊人地」，重在看后发懵的反应。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the believe root, the incredible pair and the everyday intensifier habit.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借「相信」词根、incredible 对照与日常加强语气的习惯。

normal.en: Incredibly is just incredible with -ly, the standard way English turns adjectives into adverbs.
normal.cn: incredibly 就是 incredible 加 -ly，是英语把形容词变副词的标准做法。

normal.en: Credit holds the root cred, believe, so incredibly is simply not-believably.
normal.cn: credit 里含词根 cred「相信」，所以 incredibly 就是「不可信地」。

normal.en: When someone speaks incredibly, listeners freeze for a beat before answering.
normal.cn: 有人说了难以置信的话时，听者会先愣一拍才接话。

normal.en: Most of the time it only means very, as in incredibly cheap or incredibly kind.
normal.cn: 多数时候它只表示「非常」，如 incredibly cheap（便宜得惊人）、incredibly kind（极为友善）。

normal.en: Swap in extremely and the sentence still works, only the surprise is gone.
normal.cn: 把 extremely 换进去句子照样成立，只是惊异感消失了。

abstract.en: Belief has a doorway, and some facts are simply too wide to fit through it.
abstract.cn: 相信有一道门，有些事实太宽，挤不过去。

abstract.en: Surprise is a debt language repays by turning every strong word into mild praise.
abstract.cn: 惊异是一笔债，语言用「把强烈的词磨成寻常赞美」来偿还。

abstract.en: The loudest intensifier is the one that still remembers being a doubt.
abstract.cn: 最有力的加强词，是还记得自己曾是疑问的那个。

examples.en: The city has grown incredibly quickly over the past decade.
examples.cn: 过去十年这座城市的发展快得惊人。

examples.en: He told the story so incredibly that no one could follow it.
examples.cn: 他把故事讲得离奇至极，没人听得明白。

examples.en: The mountain path is steep and incredibly dangerous in winter.
examples.cn: 这条山径陡峭，冬天危险至极。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因克瑞德利」——因账单被克扣得离谱，利润（利）令人难以置信。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ credere（相信）+ -bilis（可……的）构成 incredibilis，英语加副词后缀 -ly 得 incredibly；同根词有 incredible、credible、credit、credibility。

sensesIntro.en: Incredibly begins as the adverb of disbelief, then measures size, softens into a plain intensifier, and can still judge conduct.
sensesIntro.cn: incredibly 起初表示难以相信的方式，后来衡量大小，再磨平为普通程度副词，但仍可评判行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pause in the conversation before anyone can answer.
core.cn: 核心意象：对话里停了一拍，没人接得上话。

branches.en: TRUTH LINE: the manner itself resists belief.
branches.cn: 真伪线：方式本身抗拒被相信。

branches.en: SIZE LINE: a degree passes the limit of imagination.
branches.cn: 大小线：程度越过想象的边界。

branches.en: EMPHASIS LINE: daily speech reduces it to a plain very.
branches.cn: 强调线：日常口语把它降为普通的「非常」。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT LINE: conduct is described as too bad to accept.
branches.cn: 评判线：某种行为被描述为难以接受。

branches.en: TONE LINE: one adverb can carry shock or mere emphasis.
branches.cn: 语气线：同一个副词既可承载惊异，也可只是加强语气。

intro.en: A negative prefix on a root meaning believe, with an adjective ending and the English adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: 否定前缀加意为「相信」的词根，接形容词词尾，再加英语副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin in-, not, plus credere, to believe, plus -bilis, able to be, gave incredibilis; English added -ly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in-「不」加 credere「相信」加 -bilis「可……的」构成 incredibilis；英语再加 -ly。

items.example: the root of credible and credit
items.exampleCN: credible 与 credit 的词根

items.meaning: in a way that is hard to believe; extremely

definition_zh: 限制；限度；局限；不足之处；（法律）诉讼时效；责任限额；权利或地产的限定
definition_en: a rule or condition that limits something, and a weakness or shortcoming that a method or person cannot pass
core_image: 一条画在路面上的白线，把可以走的范围圈在里面，圈外一步也不许越
scene: 论文末尾专门用一节说明样本太小、只覆盖一所学校，提醒读者结论不能推得太远。 Every study states its limitations so that readers know how far the findings can travel.
sceneCN: 这里指研究自身的不足之处（第 4 个义项：局限、不足）；句意为每项研究都要说明自己的局限，读者才知道结论能走多远。场景图取象：路面上一条白线把可行范围圈住；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 限制；限度（可数或不可数）
局限；不足之处（多用复数）

derivatives.zh: 界限；限制（由拉丁语「边界」一词直接借入，兼指界线与设界之举）
有限的；受限制的（动词过去分词转形容词，指数量或范围受约束）
无限的；无边的（加表示「没有」的形容词后缀）
划定界限；划界（加表示「去除、划分」的前缀，指把边界明确画出）
限制性的（现在分词转形容词，指起约束作用）
无限的；不受限制的（加否定前缀，指没有设上限）

senses.title: The act of limiting
senses.definition: the act of keeping something within bounds, or the state of being kept within them
senses.definitionCN: 把某物保持在范围之内的动作，或受此约束的状态
senses.example: The limitation of outdoor gatherings began in October.
senses.exampleCN: 户外聚集的限制从十月开始。
senses.why: The noun comes from a Latin verb meaning to bound, so the act of drawing the line is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自意为「划界」的拉丁动词，画线这个动作是最古老的义项。

senses.title: A rule that restricts
senses.definition: a rule, condition or cap that restricts what may be done, used or claimed
senses.definitionCN: 限制可以做什么、用多少或主张什么的规则、条件或上限
senses.example: The contract places a limitation on how many copies may be made.
senses.exampleCN: 合同对可以制作多少份副本设了限制。
senses.why: Once a line is drawn, people need it written down, and the written line is this sense.
senses.whyCN: 线一旦画出，人们就需要把它写下来，写下来的线就是这一义项。

senses.title: A cap on money or time
senses.definition: a fixed upper amount of money, time or resources allowed for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某项用途所允许的金钱、时间或资源的固定上限
senses.example: There is a strict limitation on the daily water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 每日供水量有严格上限。
senses.why: Budgets and clocks are the most concrete boundaries, so the word settles there first.
senses.whyCN: 预算与时钟是最具体的边界，这个词先在这里落脚。

senses.title: A weakness of a method
senses.definition: a shortcoming in a study, method or tool that limits what its results can support
senses.definitionCN: 研究、方法或工具中的不足，限制了其结果能支撑的结论
senses.example: Every study states its limitations so that readers know how far the findings can travel.
senses.exampleCN: 每项研究都要说明自己的局限，读者才知道结论能走多远。
senses.why: Science uses the plural to admit what a design cannot see, and that candour is part of the method.
senses.whyCN: 科学用复数形式承认设计看不到的东西，这种坦白本身就是方法的一部分。

senses.title: The statute of limitations
senses.definition: the legal time limit within which a claim must be brought before it is barred
senses.definitionCN: 必须在期限之内提起诉讼、逾期即丧失胜诉权的法定时限
senses.example: The claim was dismissed because the limitation had expired.
senses.exampleCN: 由于时效已过，这项请求被驳回。
senses.why: Law puts a clock on every right, and the time limit is named after the limiting itself.
senses.whyCN: 法律给每项权利都装上时钟，这个时限就以「限制」这个动作为名。

senses.title: A cap on liability
senses.definition: a contractual maximum on the amount one party must pay for loss or damage
senses.definitionCN: 合同规定的、一方对损失或损害必须支付的最高金额
senses.example: The insurer accepted a limitation of liability of two million.
senses.exampleCN: 保险人接受了二百万的责任限额。
senses.why: Risk is made bearable by naming the worst number in advance, and the clause is named after that cap.
senses.whyCN: 事先把最坏的数字写出来，风险才可承受，这条款便以那个上限命名。

senses.title: A limit on an estate or right
senses.definition: a legal restriction on how long an estate or right may last or how it may pass
senses.definitionCN: 对某项地产或权利存续时间或转让方式的法定限定
senses.example: The deed carried a limitation on the sale of the land.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据对土地的出售作了限定。
senses.why: Property law inherited the Roman boundary word and uses it for estates cut down to a fixed term.
senses.whyCN: 财产法继承了罗马的边界词，用它指被限定为固定期限的产权。

senses.title: A caveat in an argument
senses.definition: a qualification attached to a claim so that it is not taken too broadly
senses.definitionCN: 附加在主张之上的限定条件，使其不被过度推广
senses.example: He added a limitation: the rule holds only for small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 他加了一个限定：这条规则只适用于小公司。
senses.why: A wise claim fences its own reach, and the fence is called a limitation.
senses.whyCN: 审慎的主张会替自己围出边界，这道围栏就叫限定。

senses.title: A boundary in space
senses.definition: an outer boundary or edge, the oldest physical sense of the root
senses.definitionCN: 外部的边界或边缘，是这个词根最古老的具体含义
senses.example: The limitation of the old city wall still shows on the map.
senses.exampleCN: 旧城墙的边界在地图上仍看得出来。
senses.why: The Latin word meant a frontier between fields, and every later sense is a descendant of that ditch.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词本指田地之间的地界，后来所有义项都是那条沟的后代。

intro.en: Limitation comes from Latin limitare 'to bound', from limes, 'boundary, frontier'. The line of descent is clear; the exact date of the English noun is uncertain.
intro.cn: limitation 来自拉丁语 limitare「划界」，出自 limes「边界、前线」。词源线索清楚，这个英语名词出现的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Limes meant a boundary line, a frontier between fields or between provinces of the empire.
items.cn: limes 意为边界线，是田地之间或帝国行省之间的分界线。

items.en: The verb limitare meant to mark a boundary and, by extension, to keep something within it.
items.cn: 动词 limitare 意为标出边界，引申为把某物留在边界之内。

items.en: Limitio and limitatio named the marking of a bound, a word of surveyors and lawyers.
items.cn: limitio 与 limitatio 指划定边界，是测量员与法律人的用语。

items.en: The noun entered English in the fifteenth century through legal and scholarly French; the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词在十五世纪经由法律与学术法语进入英语；确切年代不确定。

items.en: Modern English split the word two ways: the limitations of a study, and the limitation of liability in a contract.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词分成两支：研究的局限，以及合同中的责任限额。

items.en: The statute of limitations gave the word a clock, naming the period beyond which a right cannot be pursued.
items.cn: 诉讼时效法规给这个词装上了时钟，指超过之后权利便无法追索的期间。

note.en: The first group shares the boundary root or looks close; the second group holds the words that often stand in for limitation in argument and in law.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「边界」词根，或字形相近；第二组是论证与法律中常替代「限制、局限」的词。

entries.definition: The plain noun and verb for a boundary or a cap.
entries.definitionCN: 最朴素的边界或上限名词，也可作动词。

entries.definition: Restricted in amount or scope, the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 在数量或范围上受限制的形容词。

entries.definition: The drawing of a boundary, especially between states or fields.
entries.definitionCN: 划定边界，尤指国界或领域之间。

entries.definition: To remove something; it looks like the same family but comes from limen, a threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 清除某物；看似同族，其实出自意为「门槛」的 limen。

entries.definition: Occupying a threshold or in-between state, from limen rather than limes.
entries.definitionCN: 处于门槛或过渡状态，出自 limen 而非 limes。

entries.definition: A rule that prevents something, often imposed by authority.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止某事的规则，通常由权威施加。

entries.definition: A factor that forces a choice, close to limitation in research writing.
entries.definitionCN: 迫使作出选择的因素，在研究写作中接近「局限」。

entries.definition: A failure to reach a standard, the plain word for a weakness.
entries.definitionCN: 未能达到标准，是最朴素的「缺点」说法。

entries.definition: A disadvantage that makes something less attractive.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物吸引力下降的不利之处。

entries.definition: A warning or condition attached to a claim or permission.
entries.definitionCN: 附在主张或许可之上的警告或条件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real frontier word, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「边界」词、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Limes meant the frontier of the empire, so a limitation is a line drawn at the edge of what is allowed.
normal.cn: limes 指帝国的前线，限制就是画在允许范围边缘的一条线。

normal.en: The family runs limit, limited, limitless and delimitation.
normal.cn: 同族词有 limit、limited、limitless 与 delimitation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: limitations of the study, time limitation, limitation of liability.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：研究的局限、时间限制、责任限额。

normal.en: In law the plural has a life of its own: the statute of limitations.
normal.cn: 在法律里复数形式自成一体：诉讼时效。

normal.en: Eliminate and liminal are false friends; they come from limen, a threshold.
normal.cn: eliminate 与 liminal 是假朋友，它们出自意为门槛的 limen。

abstract.en: A limitation honestly stated is a gift to the reader, not a weakness of the writer.
abstract.cn: 老实说出的局限是给读者的礼物，而不是作者的无能。

abstract.en: Every boundary that keeps something in also keeps something out.
abstract.cn: 每道把东西圈进来的边界，也把另一些东西关在外面。

abstract.en: The line that protects also instructs; it tells you where the work begins.
abstract.cn: 起保护作用的线同时在指路，它告诉你工作从哪里开始。

examples.en: The report lists three limitations of its own method.
examples.cn: 报告列出自身方法的三处局限。

examples.en: A limitation on imports raised the price of steel.
examples.cn: 进口限制抬高了钢材价格。

examples.en: The suit was filed within the limitation period.
examples.cn: 诉讼是在时效期间内提起的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「利米泰申」——地上画一条白线，线外不许走：限制、局限

root: 拉丁语 limitare「划界」← limes「边界、前线」；经法律与学术法语于十五世纪进入英语。同族有 limit、limited、delimitation；eliminate 与 liminal 出自 limen「门槛」，属形近不同源。名词进入英语的确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all descend from one boundary: the act of bounding, a restricting rule, a cap on money or time, a weakness of method, the statute of limitations, a liability cap, a limit on an estate, a caveat in argument, and a boundary in space.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都出自同一条边界：划界之举、限制性规定、金额或时间的上限、方法的局限、诉讼时效、责任限额、对地产或权利的限定、论证中的保留，以及空间上的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white line painted across a road, with everything beyond it out of bounds.
core.cn: 核心意象：路面上画着一条白线，线外一切都不得越过。

branches.en: THE LINE ITSELF: a frontier drawn in space, and the act of drawing it.
branches.cn: 线本身：在空间里画出的边界，以及画线的动作。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN CAP: a rule or a fixed amount of money, time or water that may not be exceeded.
branches.cn: 写下来的上限：不可超过的规则，或金钱、时间、用水的定额。

branches.en: THE HONEST WEAKNESS: what a method cannot see, and the caveat that keeps a claim from spreading too far.
branches.cn: 诚实的弱点：方法看不到的东西，以及防止主张过度扩张的保留。

branches.en: THE LEGAL CLOCK AND DEED: a period after which a right is barred, and a term fixed on an estate.
branches.cn: 法律的时钟与契据：过期即失权的期间，以及为地产设定的期限。

branches.en: THE LIABILITY CAP: the worst number named in advance so that risk can be borne.
branches.cn: 责任限额：事先写出的最坏数字，好让风险可以承担。

intro.en: Limitation is a Latin boundary word turned into an abstract noun, with a family that runs through law and science.
intro.cn: limitation 是把一个拉丁边界词变成抽象名词，其词族贯穿法律与科学。

latinIntro.en: Limes and limitare are the sources; the noun ending came through Latin limitatio.
latinIntro.cn: limes 与 limitare 是来源，名词词尾经由拉丁语 limitatio 而来。

items.meaning: a marking of bounds; a restriction
items.example: The noun covers a rule, a weakness and a legal period.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词兼指规定、弱点与法定期间。

items.example: It named the edge of a field or of an empire.
items.exampleCN: 它指田地或帝国的边缘。

items.meaning: to bound, to mark a limit
items.example: The verb supplies the action behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供名词背后的动作。

items.example: It builds limitation, demarcation and estimation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成限制、划界与估计等词。

items.example: The short form is both noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 短形既可作名词也可作动词。

items.example: The participle became the everyday adjective.
items.exampleCN: 过去分词成了日常形容词。

items.example: It builds limitless, the opposite of limited.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 limitless，即 limited 的反面。

items.example: It builds delimitation, the drawing of a border.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 delimitation，即划定边界。

items.example: It builds limiting, as in a limiting factor.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 limiting，如限制因素。

latinEntries.example: Latin limes means boundary or frontier.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 limes 意为边界、前线。

latinEntries.example: Medieval Latin limitare means to mark a boundary.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 limitare 意为划定边界。

latinEntries.example: Latin limitatio means a marking of bounds.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 limitatio 意为划定界限。

definition_zh: 整洁的；井井有条的；简洁巧妙的；纯的（酒）；小巧匀称的
definition_en: tidy and in good order; simple and skilfully done; drunk without ice or water; small and well shaped
core_image: 桌面上书本按高矮排成一线，笔尖都朝同一个方向
scene: 宿舍的桌上，书本按高矮排成一线，几支笔都朝同一个方向摆着。 His desk stayed neat even during the exam week.
sceneCN: 这里是「整洁的」（第 1 个义项：摆放有序、不凌乱）；句意为即便在考试周，他的书桌也保持整洁。图中可辨识物件：书桌、书本、笔。

pos.zh: 整洁的；简洁巧妙的；纯的；小巧匀称的

derivatives.zh: 由 neat 加 -ly 构成，义为「整齐地；干净利落地」
由 neat 加 -ness 构成，义为「整洁；工整」
由 neat 加 -en 构成，义为「把……收拾整齐」

senses.title: Tidy and in good order
senses.definition: arranged carefully, with everything in its place and no clutter
senses.definitionCN: 摆放得仔细，各在其位，没有杂乱
senses.example: His desk stayed neat even during the exam week.
senses.exampleCN: 即便在考试周，他的书桌也保持整洁。
senses.why: The word came into English from French net, clean and bright, and its first job was to describe a surface with nothing spoiling it; order was the visible proof of that cleanliness.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法语 net 进入英语，本义是「干净、明亮」，最初形容没有污损的表面；整齐有序就是这种干净看得见的证据。

senses.title: Simple and skilfully done
senses.titleCN: 简洁巧妙的；干净利落的
senses.definition: done with care and skill so that the result is simple, exact and easy to follow
senses.definitionCN: 做得细致而有技巧，结果简单、准确、容易把握
senses.example: She found a neat solution that saved everyone an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 她想出一个简洁的办法，给每个人省下一小时。
senses.why: A surface is neat when nothing extra is on it, and a plan is neat when nothing extra is in it; the same dislike of clutter moves from tables to arguments.
senses.whyCN: 表面整洁是因为上面没有多余的东西，方案简洁是因为里面没有多余的步骤；同一种对杂乱的排斥，从桌面移到了论证里。

senses.title: Drunk plain, without ice or water
senses.definition: used of strong drink served on its own, with nothing added
senses.definitionCN: 用于烈酒，指单喝、不兑任何东西
senses.example: He asked for a neat whisky and sat by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他要了一杯不加冰的威士忌，坐在窗边。
senses.why: A glass with nothing added is clean in the same literal way, so the old adjective for an unspoiled surface was applied to a drink that has not been diluted.
senses.whyCN: 什么都没加的杯子，字面上同样「干净」，于是那个形容未受污损表面的旧形容词，被用到了没有兑水的酒上。

senses.title: Small, trim and well shaped
senses.definition: used of a person's body or build, meaning small, compact and pleasing in shape
senses.definitionCN: 用于人的身材，意为小巧、紧凑、比例好看
senses.example: The dancer had a neat figure and very straight posture.
senses.exampleCN: 那位舞者身材小巧匀称，姿态非常挺拔。
senses.why: A small object with clean lines looks finished rather than cramped, so neat came to praise a body built on a small scale but without awkwardness.
senses.whyCN: 线条干净的小物件看起来是完成品，而不是被挤小的；于是 neat 也用来称赞小巧却不显笨拙的身材。

intro.en: Neat came through French from a Latin adjective for something shining and polished, and English widened it from a clean surface to a clear plan and an undiluted drink.
intro.cn: neat 经法语来自一个表示「光亮、打磨过」的拉丁形容词，英语把它的词义从干净表面扩展到清晰方案与不兑水的酒。

items.en: Nitidus meant shining, bright and polished, and by extension elegant and refined in appearance.
items.cn: nitidus 意为光亮的、鲜明的、打磨过的，引申指外表雅致、精致。

items.en: The verb nitere meant to shine or to look bright, and it is the source of the adjective and of the whole family.
items.cn: 动词 nitere 意为发光、显得明亮，是这个形容词以及整族词的来源。

items.en: Old French net kept the sense of clean, clear and unspoiled, and dropped the Latin brightness into a plainer cleanliness.
items.cn: 古法语 net 保留「干净、清澈、未受污损」的意思，把拉丁语的「光亮」落成了更朴素的「干净」。

items.en: Middle English nete or neat described clean clothes, clear writing and a person who kept things in order.
items.cn: 中古英语 nete 或 neat 形容干净的衣服、清楚的字迹，以及把东西收拾得井井有条的人。

items.en: Modern English adds the praise of a simple plan, the serving of undiluted spirits and the description of a compact figure.
items.cn: 现代英语添上对简洁方案的称赞、对不兑水烈酒的用法，以及对小巧身材的描述。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adverb, the noun and the verb built on neat; the near-meaning group holds adjectives for order and for a well-kept appearance.
note.cn: 形近组收由 neat 构成的副词、名词与动词；近义组收表示「有序」与「外表收拾得好」的形容词。

entries.definition: In a tidy or skilful way, made with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 以整齐或利落的方式；由 neat 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The quality of being tidy or skilfully simple.
entries.definitionCN: 整洁或简洁巧妙的性质。

entries.definition: To make something tidy, formed with -en.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物收拾整齐；由 neat 加 -en 构成。

entries.definition: A mesh for catching things; only the spelling is close to neat.
entries.definitionCN: 用来捕捉东西的网；只是拼写与 neat 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Arranged with everything in place, often said of rooms and habits.
entries.definitionCN: 各物归位、摆放有序，常用于房间与习惯。

entries.definition: Following a clear arrangement or method, often of groups and procedures.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循清楚的安排或方法，多用于群体与程序。

entries.definition: Neat and well shaped, especially of a person or a garden.
entries.definitionCN: 整齐而外形好看，尤指人或花园。

entries.definition: Smart and clean in appearance, usually of a person dressed well.
entries.definitionCN: 外表利落干净，通常指穿着得体的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is a French cleaning word with a Latin shine behind it, and its senses all keep some idea of nothing extra.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是法语中表示「干净」的词，背后有拉丁语的「光亮」，各个义项都带着「没有多余之物」的意思。

normal.en: French net meant clean and bright, and English kept the meaning but changed the spelling to neat.
normal.cn: 法语 net 意为干净、明亮，英语保留了意思，只把拼写改成 neat。

normal.en: Latin nitidus, shining, stands behind the French word, so neat and nitid share one old picture of a polished surface.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nitidus（光亮的）站在法语词背后，所以 neat 与 nitid 共享一幅打磨过的表面画面。

normal.en: Neatly is the adverb, neatness the noun, neaten the verb; the family adds endings rather than new stems.
normal.cn: neatly 是副词，neatness 是名词，neaten 是动词；这一族只加词尾，不换词干。

normal.en: A neat solution is praised for having no extra steps, which is the same judgement as a neat desk with no extra papers.
normal.cn: a neat solution 被称赞是因为没有多余步骤，这与「没有多余纸张的整洁书桌」是同一种判断。

normal.en: Neat whisky has nothing added, so the clean-surface sense survives most literally in the glass.
normal.cn: neat whisky 什么都不加，所以「干净表面」这层意思在酒杯里保留得最字面。

abstract.en: Cleanliness, brightness and order turn out to be three views of one surface with nothing on it that should not be there.
abstract.cn: 干净、光亮与有序，其实只是同一个表面的三个视角：上面没有不该有的东西。

abstract.en: A word that began by praising a polished table ends up praising a proof with no wasted line.
abstract.cn: 一个从称赞打磨过的桌面开始的词，最后用来称赞没有一句废话的证明。

abstract.en: Serving a drink neat is the same compliment as keeping a desk neat: nothing has been added.
abstract.cn: 把酒纯着端上来，与把桌子收拾整齐是同一种称赞：什么都没有往里加。

examples.en: Her handwriting is small and very neat.
examples.cn: 她的字小而工整。

examples.en: He keeps his tools in a neat row on the shelf.
examples.cn: 他把工具在架子上排成整齐的一列。

examples.en: The team needed a neat way to explain the result.
examples.cn: 团队需要一个简洁的方式来解释这个结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼特」——东西摆得利落，一眼看过去清清爽爽；neat 就是整洁的。

root: 古法语 net（干净、明亮）来自拉丁语 nitidus（光亮的），一般认为与动词 nitere（发光）同源；本义「干净明亮」，后引申出整洁、简洁、纯饮与小巧诸义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a surface with nothing extra on it; order, simplicity, an undiluted drink and a compact figure are four ways that emptiness of extras shows itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「没有多余之物的表面」；有序、简洁、不兑水的酒与小巧的身材，是这种「无多余」显现出来的四种方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: books standing in one straight line on a desk, pens all pointing the same way.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的书排成一条直线，笔尖全都朝着同一个方向。

branches.en: a shelf where every tool has its place
branches.cn: 每件工具都有位置的架子

branches.en: a page of writing without a smudge
branches.cn: 没有一处污痕的字页

branches.en: a proof that fits on one blackboard
branches.cn: 一块黑板就写得下的证明

branches.en: a glass filled and left alone
branches.cn: 斟满之后不再动的一只杯子

branches.en: a dancer standing very straight
branches.cn: 站得笔直的舞者

intro.en: The word is a French adjective of cleanliness, a Latin adjective of shine, and the English endings that turn it into adverb, noun and verb.
intro.cn: 这个词由法语表示「干净」的形容词、拉丁语表示「光亮」的形容词，以及把它变成副词、名词与动词的英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplied the adjective of shine and the verb behind it, and French passed the cleaned-up sense to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示「光亮」的形容词及其动词，法语把「干净」这层意思传给了英语。

items.meaningCN: 光亮的；打磨过的；雅致的

items.meaning: in a tidy or skilful way

latinEntries.meaningCN: 光亮的；打磨过的；整洁的

definition_zh: 获得；得到；取得；赢得；（古）握有；（规则、习俗）通行
definition_en: to get or acquire something, especially through effort, request, or established right
core_image: 伸手向前，抓住一件东西并握牢
scene: 研究者在一间政府办事窗口等了两小时，就为拿到一张签了字的许可。 A researcher waits at a government office window for two hours to obtain a signed permit.
sceneCN: 这里 obtain 是「取得、拿到」（第 2 个义项：通过努力或申请得到）；句意：研究人员在政府办事窗口等了两个小时，才取得一份签好字的许可证。图中可辨识物件：许可证、办事窗口、印章、签字笔、排号单；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Take Hold: come to have something
senses.titleCN: 抓住：使某物归自己所有
senses.definition: to get or acquire something so that it becomes yours
senses.definitionCN: 得到或取得某物，使之归自己所有
senses.example: She obtained a copy of the report from the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 她从档案馆取得了一份报告副本。
senses.why: Latin obtinere joined ob- 'in front of' to tenere 'to hold'. The first sense is physical: you reach forward and close your hand on something, so obtain means to get it into your possession.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obtinere 把 ob-“在前”加在 tenere“握持”上。第一个义项是身体性的：你向前伸手，把东西握在手里，于是 obtain 意为“使某物进入自己的占有”。

senses.title: Earn the Hold: secure through effort
senses.titleCN: 挣得握持：通过努力取得
senses.definition: to succeed in getting something after effort, application, or negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力、申请或协商后成功得到某物
senses.example: It took three meetings to obtain the funding.
senses.exampleCN: 取得这笔资金开了三次会。
senses.why: A grip that must be worked for is still a grip. The hand reaches farther and closes later, so obtain adds the idea of effort to plain getting.
senses.whyCN: 需要费力才得到的握持仍然是握持。手伸得更远、合拢得更晚，于是 obtain 在“得到”之上加了“付出努力”的意思。

senses.title: Come By It: inherit or receive
senses.definition: in older use, to come into possession of something by inheritance or by receiving it
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指通过继承或受赠而占有某物
senses.example: He obtained the land from his father.
senses.exampleCN: 他从父亲那里继承了这块土地。
senses.why: The early French and Latin record lists 'inherit' among the senses of obtain. The thing still passes into your hold, but the reaching is done by family or gift rather than by effort.
senses.whyCN: 早期法语和拉丁语记录把“继承”列为 obtain 的义项之一。东西仍然进入你的握持，但伸手的是家族或赠予，而不是努力。

senses.title: Win the Field: obtain a victory
senses.definition: to gain or win something such as a victory, advantage, or right, often against opposition
senses.definitionCN: 赢得胜利、优势或权利等，常指对抗之中取得
senses.example: The small force obtained a decisive victory at the pass.
senses.exampleCN: 这支小部队在隘口取得了决定性胜利。
senses.why: Early records also give 'conquer' as a sense. To obtain a victory is to take hold of the outcome after struggle, the same grip won against someone else.
senses.whyCN: 早期记录还给出“征服”义。obtain a victory 就是在争斗之后握住结果，是同一只从对手那里赢来的手。

senses.title: Hold Fast: the archaic sense of possession
senses.titleCN: 握牢不放：古老的占有义
senses.definition: in archaic use, to hold, keep, or possess something rather than to get it
senses.definitionCN: 古旧用法，指握持、保留或占有某物，而不是“得到”
senses.example: The old charter says the family shall obtain the manor for a thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 那份古老契据说，该家族应握有这座庄园一千年。
senses.why: Obtinere in Latin could mean 'hold fast' as well as 'get possession of'. English kept the holding sense for a while: the hand is already closed and stays closed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obtinere 既可指“握牢”，也可指“取得占有”。英语一度保留了“握持”义：手已经合拢，并且一直不松开。

senses.title: The Custom Obtains: be current in practice
senses.titleCN: 习俗通行：在实际中成立
senses.definition: to be prevalent or customary, to be established in practice, used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 盛行或成为惯例，在实际中确立，作不及物动词
senses.example: The custom still obtains in the mountain villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗在山村里仍然通行。
senses.why: From the 1610s the intransitive sense appears. A practice that 'holds' among people is one that grips the community, so obtain comes to mean 'be current'.
senses.whyCN: 不及物义自 17 世纪 10 年代出现。一种做法在人群中“握得住”，就是抓住了整个社群，于是 obtain 意为“通行、成立”。

senses.title: Obtain Permission: the formal request
senses.definition: to succeed in getting official permission, consent, or approval through the proper channel
senses.definitionCN: 通过正当渠道成功取得官方许可、同意或批准
senses.example: You must obtain written consent before using the photographs.
senses.exampleCN: 使用这些照片前必须取得书面同意。
senses.why: Here the grip is granted by an authority. You put a request forward, the office puts a signed paper forward, and the paper passes into your hand.
senses.whyCN: 这里的握持由权力机构授予。你把申请递到前面，办事窗口把签好的文件递到前面，文件最终进入你的手中。

senses.title: Obtain Data: gather what is out there
senses.titleCN: 获取数据：把在外面的东西取回
senses.definition: to get information, measurements, or evidence, often by going to the source
senses.definitionCN: 取得信息、测量值或证据，常指到源头去取
senses.example: The team obtained samples from twelve different sites.
senses.exampleCN: 团队从十二个不同地点取得了样本。
senses.why: Data exist outside you and must be brought into reach. The old forward reach fits research: you go to the source, take the reading, and hold it as a record.
senses.whyCN: 数据存在于你之外，必须被带进可及范围。古老的“向前伸手”正适合研究：你到源头去，取回读数，并把它作为记录握在手里。

senses.title: Obtain a Degree: earn a standing
senses.titleCN: 取得学位：挣得一种资格
senses.definition: to complete the requirements for and receive a qualification, degree, or position
senses.definitionCN: 完成要求并取得资格、学位或职位
senses.example: She obtained her doctorate after six years of research.
senses.exampleCN: 经过六年研究，她取得了博士学位。
senses.why: A degree is conferred after requirements are met, yet it still enters your hold. The thing obtained here is a standing you can keep and carry.
senses.whyCN: 学位是在满足要求后授予的，但它仍然进入你的握持。这里取得的东西是一种你可以保有并带走的身份资格。

intro.en: Obtain entered English in the early 15th century from Old French obtenir or directly from Latin obtinere 'hold fast, get possession of'. The holding image in tenere is the core, and the intransitive 'be prevalent' sense followed in the 1610s.
intro.cn: obtain 于 15 世纪初从古法语 obtenir 或直接拉丁语 obtinere“握牢、取得占有”进入英语。tenere 的“握持”意象是核心，不及物的“通行”义则于 17 世纪 10 年代出现。

items.en: Recorded as obteinen, meaning 'to get or acquire, inherit, gain, conquer'.
items.cn: 以 obteinen 形式记录，意为“得到或取得、继承、获得、征服”。

items.en: From Old French obtenir (14c.) or directly from Latin obtinere 'hold, hold fast, take hold of, get possession of, acquire'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 obtenir（14 世纪），或直接来自拉丁语 obtinere“握持、握牢、抓住、取得占有、获得”。

items.en: Obtinere is ob- 'in front of' (here possibly intensive) plus tenere 'to hold'.
items.cn: obtinere 是 ob-“在前”（此处也可能是强调用法）加 tenere“握持”。

items.en: Tenere is generally traced to PIE *ten- 'to stretch', the same root family as tenant and tenacity.
items.cn: tenere 一般认为可追到原始印欧语 *ten-“伸展”，与 tenant、tenacity 同属一个词根家族。

items.en: The intransitive sense 'be prevalent or customary, be established in practice' is recorded.
items.cn: 记录到不及物义“盛行或成为惯例、在实际中确立”。

items.en: The verb yields obtainable, unobtainable, obtainment and obtainer. Its ob- prefix is shared with occupy (ob- + capere 'seize') and occur (ob- + currere 'run'), but the roots differ.
items.cn: 这个动词派生出 obtainable、unobtainable、obtainment、obtainer。它的 ob- 前缀与 occupy（ob- + capere“抓取”）、occur（ob- + currere“跑”）相同，但词根不同。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the -tain ending; the near-meaning group holds words that approach 'get' from different angles.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 -tain 结尾；近义组是从不同角度接近“得到”的词。

entries.definition: to hold inside. It shares tenere 'to hold' with obtain, but con- means 'together', so the holding is inward.
entries.definitionCN: 容纳；包含。它与 obtain 共用 tenere“握持”，但 con- 意为“一起”，握持方向朝内。

entries.definition: to keep or continue to hold. The re- prefix points back, so the grip stays rather than being newly acquired.
entries.definitionCN: 保留；继续握有。前缀 re- 指向回，握持是留在手里，而不是新取得。

entries.definition: to reach or achieve. It looks like obtain but comes from ad- plus tangere 'to touch', not from tenere.
entries.definitionCN: 达到；获得。它看起来像 obtain，但来自 ad- 加 tangere“触摸”，不是 tenere。

entries.definition: to get or come to possess something, often over time. It is more formal than obtain and stresses the process.
entries.definitionCN: 取得；逐渐占有。它比 obtain 更正式，更强调过程。

entries.definition: to get something useful or advantageous. It often implies an increase, while obtain is neutral about value.
entries.definitionCN: 获得（有用或有利的东西）。它常含“增加”，obtain 对价值是中性的。

entries.definition: to get something after effort and make it safe to keep. It adds certainty to the plain act of obtaining.
entries.definitionCN: 经过努力取得并确保保住。它在“得到”之上加了“确保”。

normalIntro.en: Real links only: ob- plus tenere 'to hold', the -tain family of contain, retain and sustain, and the fixed phrase 'the custom obtains'.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实联系：ob- 加 tenere“握持”、contain／retain／sustain 的 -tain 词族，以及固定说法 the custom obtains。

normal.en: Ob- 'in front of' plus tenere 'to hold' makes obtain: to get a hold of something.
normal.cn: ob-“在前”加 tenere“握持”构成 obtain：抓住某物、取得握持。

normal.en: Contain, retain and sustain all share tenere; only the prefix tells you which direction the holding goes.
normal.cn: contain、retain、sustain 都共用 tenere；只有前缀告诉你握持的方向。

normal.en: Obtain, occupy and occur share ob-, but their roots differ: tenere 'hold', capere 'seize', currere 'run'.
normal.cn: obtain、occupy、occur 共用 ob-，但词根不同：tenere“握”、capere“抓”、currere“跑”。

normal.en: Obtain permission is the standard formal frame for an official yes.
normal.cn: obtain permission 是取得官方许可的标准正式搭配。

normal.en: The custom obtains is the intransitive survivor: a practice holds among people.
normal.cn: the custom obtains 是不及物义的存留：一种做法在人群中握得住。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching forward and closing around a handle; the handle is now yours to keep.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手向前伸出，握住一个把手；这个把手现在归你保有。

abstract.en: The same grip can be laid on a custom: a practice holds a whole community in place.
abstract.cn: 同一只握持的手可以放在习俗上：一种做法把整个社群握在原地。

abstract.en: At a counter, a signed paper slides forward into your hand: obtaining is that moment of transfer.
abstract.cn: 在办事窗口，一份签好的文件滑向前方、进入你手中：obtain 就是交接的那一刻。

examples.en: The laboratory obtained the samples from three rivers in the region.
examples.cn: 实验室从该地区的三条河流取得了样本。

examples.en: Students must obtain permission before filming inside the museum.
examples.cn: 学生在博物馆内拍摄前必须获得许可。

examples.en: That rule no longer obtains in most modern cities.
examples.cn: 那条规则在大多数现代城市已不再通行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额不，抬恩」——伸手一抬，把恩赐的东西接住 → obtain 获得、取得

root: 拉丁语 obtinere“握牢、取得占有”= ob“在前”+ tenere“握持”（一般认为追到原始印欧语 *ten-“伸展”）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of obtain all keep one gesture: a hand reaches forward and closes. It can close on an object, a victory, a permission, a set of data, a degree, or even a custom that holds a community.
sensesIntro.cn: obtain 的九个义项都保留同一个动作：手向前伸出并合拢。它握住的可以是物件、胜利、许可、数据、学位，甚至一种握住了社群的习俗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching forward and closing on something.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手向前伸出，把某物握在掌中。

branches.en: COMING TO HAVE: acquiring something, and receiving it by inheritance.
branches.cn: 归于己有：取得某物，以及通过继承得到。

branches.en: CONTESTED GAINS: securing something by effort, and winning a victory.
branches.cn: 争夺而得：靠努力取得，以及赢得胜利。

branches.en: HOLDING FAST: the archaic sense of keeping what is already in hand.
branches.cn: 握牢不放：保留手中已有之物的古义。

branches.en: HOLDING AMONG PEOPLE: a custom or rule that obtains, still current.
branches.cn: 在人群中成立：仍然通行的习俗或规则。

branches.en: FORMAL ACQUISITION: permission, data, and a qualification all pass into your hold.
branches.cn: 正式取得：许可、数据和学位资格都进入你的握持。

intro.en: Obtain is ob- plus the Latin root tenere 'to hold'. English adds -able, -ment and -er, while the same -tain root appears in contain, retain, sustain, tenant and maintain.
intro.cn: obtain 是 ob- 加拉丁词根 tenere“握持”。英语加 -able、-ment、-er，而同一个 -tain 词根出现在 contain、retain、sustain、tenant、maintain 中。

latinIntro.en: Latin obtinere 'hold fast, get possession' is ob- plus tenere 'to hold'. Tenere is generally traced to PIE *ten- 'to stretch'; it is not related to capere 'seize' or currere 'run', which build occupy and occur.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 obtinere“握牢、取得占有”是 ob- 加 tenere“握持”。tenere 一般认为追到原始印欧语 *ten-“伸展”；它与 capere“抓取”、currere“跑”无关，后两者构成 occupy 和 occur。

items.meaning: to get a hold of; to acquire
items.meaningCN: 抓住；获得（ob-“在前”+ tenere“握持”）
items.example: They obtained the land through a legal purchase.
items.exampleCN: 他们通过合法购买取得了这片土地。

items.meaningCN: 可获得的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: The tickets are obtainable only at the door.
The rare mineral is almost unobtainable now.
items.exampleCN: 这种稀有矿物如今几乎无法获得。

items.meaningCN: 获得；取得（-ment 构成动作名词）
items.example: The obtainment of a visa took several weeks.

items.meaningCN: 获得者；取得者（-er 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The first obtainer of the map was a naval officer.
items.exampleCN: 第一个得到这张地图的人是一名海军军官。

items.meaningCN: 容纳；包含（con-“一起”+ tenere“握持”）

items.meaning: to keep or continue to hold
items.example: The soil retains water after rain.

items.structure: sus- (sub-, from below) + tain (tenere, to hold)
items.meaning: to hold up or keep going
items.meaningCN: 支撑；维持（sus- 即 sub-“在下”+ tenere）
items.example: The beams sustain the weight of the roof.
items.exampleCN: 这些梁支撑着屋顶的重量。

items.meaning: a person who holds a lease
items.meaningCN: 租户；房客（ten-“握持”+ -ant 表示人）
items.example: The tenant pays rent on the first day of the month.
items.exampleCN: 租户在每月第一天交房租。

items.meaning: to keep in good condition; to hold a view
items.meaningCN: 维持；保养；坚持（manu“手”+ tenere“握持”）
items.example: The crew maintains the bridge every summer.
items.exampleCN: 养路队每年夏天维护这座桥。

latinEntries.meaning: hold, hold fast, take hold of, get possession of, acquire
latinEntries.meaningCN: 握持；握牢；抓住；取得占有；获得
握；持；抓住（一般认为追到原始印欧语 *ten-“伸展”）

definition_zh: 实施；执行；贯彻；（名词）工具、器具
definition_en: to put a plan or decision into effect, or a tool used for a particular job
core_image: 钉在车间墙上的新流程图，旁边挂着一把扳手
scene: 新规定贴在门口，第二周真的开始执行了。 Once the manager decided to implement the safety rules, every worker had to sign the sheet before entering.
sceneCN: 这里 implement 是「实施、执行」（第 1 个义项：把计划变为实际做法），句意是经理一旦决定实施安全规定，每个工人进门前都要在表上签到。画面里有门口贴的新规定和墙上的流程图。

derivatives.zh: （形近）作为工具或手段的、辅助实施的

senses.title: To carry a plan into effect
senses.definition: to take a decision, rule or plan and make it work in practice
senses.definitionCN: 把决定、规定或计划真正落实为做法
senses.example: The school will implement the new timetable in March.
senses.exampleCN: 学校将在三月实施新的课表。
senses.why: The Latin root means to fill up, and carrying out a plan fills the gap between intention and fact.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「填满」，而落实计划正是把「打算」与「事实」之间的空隙填满。

senses.title: A tool for a task
senses.definition: an object used to carry out a particular kind of work
senses.definitionCN: 用于完成某类工作的物件
senses.example: Old farm implements hang in the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 谷仓里挂着旧农具。
senses.why: A tool is what supplies a job with what it needs, so the filling root named the thing that fills the lack.
senses.whyCN: 工具正是为工作补上所缺之物，因此那个表示「填满」的词根也命名了补缺的物件。

senses.title: To put into practice as a duty
senses.definition: used of officials whose job is to make rules real
senses.definitionCN: 用于负责把规则落到实处的人员
senses.example: Inspectors must implement the standards without favour.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员必须不偏不倚地贯彻这些标准。
senses.why: When an institution delegates execution, the verb takes an official subject and gains a tone of duty.
senses.whyCN: 当机构把执行权委派下去时，这个动词的主语多为官方人员，语气带上职责感。

intro.en: Implement is built on a Latin verb meaning to fill up, and both tool and execution grow from that idea of supplying what is missing.
intro.cn: implement 建立在拉丁语「填满」动词之上，工具与执行两种用法都从「补上所缺」这一想法长出。

items.en: Plere meant to fill, and its root sits inside plenus, full.
items.cn: 拉丁语 plere 意为填满，其词根也藏在 plenus（满的）之中。

items.en: Implere meant to fill up completely, to complete what was lacking.
items.cn: implere 意为彻底填满，把所缺的部分补齐。

items.en: Its participle impletum, with the noun implementum, named a filling and later a thing that fills a need.
items.cn: 其分词 impletum 与名词 implementum 指充填，后指满足需要的物件。

items.en: English took implement as a noun for equipment in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语以名词形式引入 implement，指装备器具。

items.en: The verb came much later, and in the twentieth century business and government made implement a standard word for carrying out policy.
items.cn: 动词用法出现得晚得多，二十世纪企业与政府把 implement 变成「执行政策」的标准词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the filling root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of carrying out.
note.cn: 形近组收「填满」词根的词；近义组收表示执行的动词。

entries.definition: The act of putting a plan into practice.
entries.definitionCN: 把计划付诸实行的行为。

entries.definition: Something that completes another, from the same filling root.
entries.definitionCN: 补足另一物之物，同出「填满」之根。

entries.definition: Fully filled, with nothing missing.
entries.definitionCN: 完全填满、一无所缺的。

entries.definition: To do what was planned, in plain everyday words.
entries.definitionCN: 把计划好的事做出来，最朴素的说法。

entries.definition: To perform a plan or order, often with legal or military weight.
entries.definitionCN: 执行计划或命令，常带法律或军事语气。

entries.definition: To put a rule or method to practical use.
entries.definitionCN: 把规则或方法用到实际中。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the filling root to a wrench on the wall and to a policy that must reach the shop floor.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把「填满」词根连到墙上的扳手和必须落到车间的政策上。

normal.en: Im- in, ple- fill: implement is to fill the plan in with action.
normal.cn: im- 向内，ple- 填满：implement 就是把行动填进计划里。

normal.en: The verb stresses the first syllable in British English: IM-ple-ment.
normal.cn: 英式英语里动词重音在前：IM-ple-ment。

normal.en: Noun and verb share a spelling, unlike complement with an e.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，注意别与带 e 的 complement 混淆。

normal.en: A tool is what fills your hand with what the job needs.
normal.cn: 工具就是把干活所需之物填进你手里的东西。

normal.en: Policies are written in offices but implemented in shops and schools.
normal.cn: 政策写在办公室里，却是实施在店铺与学校里。

abstract.en: The word names the hardest half of any reform, the part after the announcement.
abstract.cn: 这个词命名的是一切改革中最难的那一半，即宣布之后的部分。

abstract.en: Its two senses meet in one idea: something missing gets supplied, by a hand tool or by a bureaucrat.
abstract.cn: 两个义项在一个想法里相遇：缺什么补什么，或用手里的工具，或用公职人员。

abstract.en: A good plan unimplemented is only a hope written down.
abstract.cn: 未能落地的良策，只是写下来的愿望。

examples.en: The government promised to implement the report's advice.
examples.cn: 政府承诺落实报告中的建议。

examples.en: Implementing the change took three months of training.
examples.cn: 实施这项变动花了三个月培训。

examples.en: Simple stone implements were found in the cave.
examples.cn: 洞中发现了简单的石制器具。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 使 + ple 填满 + ment 名词/动词尾——把空缺填满：实施；能补上所需之物的工具

root: 拉丁语 implere「填满」→ 分词 impletum、名词 implementum，十五世纪进入英语作名词「器具」，二十世纪衍生动词「实施」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: carrying out a plan, the tool used for work, and the official duty of making rules real.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：落实计划、干活用的工具，以及把规定真正落地的职务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a policy poster on a factory door beside a wrench hanging on a nail.
core.cn: 核心意象：车间门口的政策告示，旁边的钉子上挂着一把扳手。

branches.en: THE OFFICE LINE: timetables and rules turn into actions.
branches.cn: 办公室线：课表与规定变成实际行动。

branches.en: THE BARN LINE: implements hang where farm work happens.
branches.cn: 谷仓线：农具挂在真正做农活的地方。

branches.en: THE DUTY LINE: inspectors implement standards without favour.
branches.cn: 职责线：检查员不偏不倚地贯彻标准。

branches.en: THE HANDS LINE: tools fill the hands, plans fill the calendar.
branches.cn: 手边线：工具填满双手，计划填满日程。

branches.en: THE FOLLOW-UP LINE: both name the work that comes after the decision.
branches.cn: 后续线：两者指的都是决定之后的活儿。

intro.en: Implement is a Latin filling verb turned English noun and then verb again, with a family of completion words.
intro.cn: implement 是拉丁语「填满」动词先变英语名词、再变动词，身边是一族「完备」词。

latinIntro.en: Plere and implere are recorded in Latin, and the participle supplies the English stem.
latinIntro.cn: plere 与 implere 均有拉丁文献，其分词提供了英语词干。

items.meaningCN: 表示物或结果的名词词尾

items.meaning: a tool; to put into effect
items.example: They implemented the plan at once.
The scheme was implemented last year.

items.meaning: the carrying out of a plan
something added to fill a lack

latinEntries.meaning: a filling, a means of filling

definition_zh: 版本；版次；一期；一版（发行量）
definition_en: a particular version of a book, newspaper or broadcast, or the total number of copies produced at one time
core_image: 同一本书在桌上排成几摞，封面颜色各不相同
scene: 同一本书在桌上排成几摞，封面颜色各不相同。 The first edition sold out within a week.
sceneCN: 这里 edition 是「版本」（第 1 个义项：同一作品的一次具体出版形式）；句意为第一版一周内售罄。图中可辨识物件：几摞书、不同封面、售罄标签。

pos.zh: 名词：版本；版次；一期；一版发行量

derivatives.zh: 由本词词干加指人后缀构成，义为「编辑」
由本词词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「编辑的；社论」
由本词词干构成，义为「编辑；剪辑」

senses.title: A version of a published work
senses.titleCN: 版本：同一作品的一次出版形式
senses.definition: a particular form in which a book, magazine or other work is published, differing from other forms in content, size or cover
senses.definitionCN: 书、杂志或其他作品出版时的一种具体形式，在内容、开本或封面上与其他形式不同
senses.example: The first edition sold out within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 第一版一周内售罄。
senses.why: Latin editio meant a bringing forth; a version is what a publisher brings out at one moment, with its own text and shape.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 editio 意为「拿出、产出」；版本就是出版者在某一时刻拿出来的东西，有自己的文本与形态。

senses.title: One print run
senses.definition: the whole number of copies of a work printed and issued at one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次印刷并发行的一件作品的全部册数
senses.example: The library bought the entire edition of the new atlas.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆买下了新地图册的整版印量。
senses.why: The act of bringing forth produces a batch, and the batch itself took the name of the act.
senses.whyCN: 「拿出」这一动作会产生一批东西，而这一批东西本身就沿用了动作的名称。

senses.title: A regular version of a broadcast
senses.titleCN: 一期：定期出版或播出的一个版本
senses.definition: one of the regular forms of a newspaper, programme or broadcast, such as an evening edition
senses.definitionCN: 报纸、节目或广播的常规形式之一，如晚报版
senses.example: The evening edition carries the closing stock prices.
senses.exampleCN: 晚报版刊登收盘股价。
senses.why: A daily paper brings forth a new version each day, so each issue is another edition of the same title.
senses.whyCN: 日报每天拿出一个新版本，所以每一期都是同一报名下的又一次 edition。

intro.en: Edition comes from Latin verbs of giving out, and its whole family is built on the idea of bringing something forth.
intro.cn: edition 来自拉丁语中「拿出、发出」的动词，整个词族都围绕「把东西拿出来」这一想法。

items.en: Dare meant to give, and it supplied the second element of the publishing verbs.
items.cn: dare 意为「给」，为出版类动词提供第二个成分。

items.en: E plus dare formed edere, 'to give out, bring forth, publish'.
items.cn: e- 加 dare 构成 edere，意为「发出、拿出、出版」。

items.en: Editio was the noun of that act, a bringing forth or a publication.
items.cn: editio 是这一动作的名词，意为「拿出、出版」。

items.en: French passed the word to English, where it narrowed to a published version.
items.cn: 法语把这个词传给英语，在英语中窄化为「已出版的版本」。

items.en: Printing and broadcasting added the senses of a print run and a regular issue.
items.cn: 印刷与广播又加入了「印量」与「定期一期」两义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the publishing family; the near-meaning group gathers words for versions and copies.
note.cn: 形近组收出版词族；近义组收表示版本与册本的词。

entries.definition: A person who prepares text or a publication for issue.
entries.definitionCN: 为出版而整理文本或出版物的人。

entries.definition: An adjective for editing, or a newspaper's opinion article.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指编辑的；也指报纸的评论文章。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to prepare or correct text, film or sound.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为编辑或剪辑文本、影像与声音。

entries.definition: A form of something that differs from other forms of it.
entries.definitionCN: 与同一事物的其他形式有所不同的一个形式。

entries.definition: One number of a magazine or newspaper, or a set of items issued together.
entries.definitionCN: 杂志或报纸的一期，或一起发行的一套物品。

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a stack of covers to one print run and then to the evening paper.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一摞封面，走到一次印量，再到晚报。

normal.en: Edition is a bringing forth: the publisher brings a version out.
normal.cn: edition 就是「拿出来」：出版者把一个版本拿出来。

normal.en: Same title, different cover: that is a new edition, not a new book.
normal.cn: 同一书名，不同封面：那是新版本，不是新书。

normal.en: One printing makes one edition, counted in copies.
normal.cn: 一次印刷构成一个版次，以册数计算。

normal.en: A daily paper is a new edition every day, which is why we say evening edition.
normal.cn: 日报每天都是新的一版，所以我们说 evening edition。

normal.en: Edition, editor and edit all come from the same giving-out verb.
normal.cn: edition、editor、edit 都来自同一个表示「拿出」的动词。

abstract.en: Picture several stacks of one book, each cover a different colour.
abstract.cn: 想象同一本书的几摞，每摞封面颜色不同。

abstract.en: The same stack can be a revised text, a print run, or today's paper.
abstract.cn: 同一摞书可以是一个修订文本、一次印量，或今天的报纸。

abstract.en: Edition means the same work put out again in a new form.
abstract.cn: edition 意味着同一作品以新形态再次出版。

examples.en: The first edition sold out within a week.
examples.cn: 第一版一周内售罄。

examples.en: The library bought the entire edition of the new atlas.
examples.cn: 图书馆买下了新地图册的整版印量。

examples.en: The evening edition carries the closing stock prices.
examples.cn: 晚报版刊登收盘股价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊迪申」——同一本书几摞，封面颜色不同

root: 拉丁语 editio「拿出、出版」由 e-「出」加 dare「给」构成的 edere 派生；经法语 édition 进入英语，后扩展为印量与定期一版。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of edition: a version of a work, the number of copies printed at one time, and one regular issue of a paper or programme.
sensesIntro.cn: edition 的三个义项：作品的一种版本、一次印刷的册数，以及报纸或节目的一期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several stacks of one book, each with a differently coloured cover.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一本书的几摞，每摞封面颜色不同。

branches.en: THE VERSION: one published form of a work.
branches.cn: 版本线：一件作品的一种出版形态。

branches.en: THE RUN: the whole batch printed at one time.
branches.cn: 印量线：一次印出的整批册数。

branches.en: THE ISSUE: one regular version of a paper or programme.
branches.cn: 一期线：报纸或节目的一次常规版本。

branches.en: THE REPETITION: both are the same title brought out again.
branches.cn: 重复线：两者都是同一标题再次拿出。

branches.en: THE BATCH: a version exists as the copies actually produced.
branches.cn: 批次线：版本以实际印出的册数而存在。

intro.en: Edition is a Latin-derived noun; English adds person and adjective endings to the same stem.
intro.cn: edition 是源自拉丁语的名词，英语在同一词干上加指人与形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin dare, edere and editio are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dare、edere 与 editio 均有记录，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.exampleCN: 它与 dare 构成 edere。

items.example: The verb is the source of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族的来源。

items.example: It is the direct source of edition.

definition_zh: 原谅；宽恕；免除；请原谅
definition_en: to stop being angry with someone, to pardon a wrong, to cancel a debt, or to ask politely
core_image: 紧握的拳头慢慢松开，怒气像沙子一样漏掉
scene: 她原谅了他的迟到。 She forgave him for being late.
sceneCN: 这里 forgive 是「原谅」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她原谅了他的迟到。

senses.title: To stop being angry
senses.definition: to stop being angry with someone for a wrong
senses.definitionCN: 因某人的过错而不再生气
senses.example: She forgave him for being late.
senses.exampleCN: 她原谅了他的迟到。
senses.why: This is the everyday personal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的人际义项。

senses.title: To pardon
senses.definition: to pardon a serious wrong or crime
senses.definitionCN: 宽恕严重的过错或罪行
senses.example: The king forgave the prisoner.
senses.exampleCN: 国王宽恕了那名囚犯。
senses.why: The word can carry the weight of law.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以承载法律的重量。

senses.title: To cancel a debt
senses.definition: to officially cancel money that is owed
senses.definitionCN: 正式取消所欠的钱
senses.example: The bank forgave the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 银行免除了这笔贷款。
senses.why: A debt can be released like a grudge.
senses.whyCN: 债务可以像怨恨一样被释放。

senses.title: A polite opener
senses.definition: used politely before asking or interrupting
senses.definitionCN: 在提问或打断之前礼貌使用
senses.example: Forgive me, but I have a question.
senses.exampleCN: 请原谅，我有个问题。
senses.why: The pardon sense softens everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 宽恕义项让日常言语变得柔和。

intro.en: Forgive originally meant to give up a claim or a debt.
intro.cn: forgive 最初意为放弃一项要求或债务。

items.en: Forgyfan meant to give up or pardon.
items.cn: forgyfan 意为放弃或宽恕。

items.en: Forgiven kept the sense of pardon.
items.cn: forgiven 保留了宽恕的含义。

items.en: The idea extended from wrongs to debts.
items.cn: 这个概念从过错扩展到债务。

items.en: Forgiveness became a common noun.
items.cn: forgiveness 成为常见名词。

items.en: The polite phrase forgive me developed.
items.cn: 礼貌用语 forgive me 发展起来。

note.en: Forgive is compared with similar-looking words and with words for pardoning.
note.cn: 把 forgive 与形近词以及表示宽恕的词作比较。

entries.definition: to fail to remember
entries.definitionCN: 忘记

entries.definition: to shape metal or fake
entries.definitionCN: 锻造；伪造

entries.definition: to choose not to have
entries.definitionCN: 放弃

entries.definition: to forgive a wrong
entries.definitionCN: 原谅；赦免

entries.definition: to forgive a small fault
entries.definitionCN: 原谅小过失

entries.definition: to declare someone free of blame
entries.definitionCN: 赦免

normalIntro.en: To forgive is to open a hand that was holding a grudge.
normalIntro.cn: forgive 就是松开那只攥着怨恨的手。

normal.en: She forgave him for being late.
normal.cn: 她原谅了他的迟到。

normal.en: The king forgave the prisoner.
normal.cn: 国王宽恕了那名囚犯。

normal.en: The bank forgave the loan.
normal.cn: 银行免除了这笔贷款。

normal.en: Forgive me, but I have a question.
normal.cn: 请原谅，我有个问题。

normal.en: It is hard to forgive a lie.
normal.cn: 原谅一个谎言很难。

abstract.en: Forgiveness frees two people at once.
abstract.cn: 宽恕同时释放两个人。

abstract.en: To forgive is not to forget.
abstract.cn: 原谅并不等于忘记。

abstract.en: A forgiven debt leaves no shadow.
abstract.cn: 被免除的债务不会留下阴影。

examples.en: She forgave him for being late.
examples.cn: 她原谅了他的迟到。

examples.en: The king forgave the prisoner.
examples.cn: 国王宽恕了那名囚犯。

examples.en: It is hard to forgive a lie.
examples.cn: 原谅一个谎言很难。

dict_mnemonic.text: forgive 就是 for（彻底）加 give（给出去）：把怨恨彻底给出去，自己就轻松了。

root: 源自古英语 forgyfan（彻底给予、放弃），核心义「放下追讨，把怨恨或债务给出去」。

sensesIntro.en: Forgive means to stop being angry, to pardon, to cancel a debt, or to speak politely.
sensesIntro.cn: forgive 意为原谅、宽恕、免除或请原谅。

core.en: Letting go of a claim against someone.
core.cn: 放弃对某人的追讨。

branches.en: The anger is put down.
branches.cn: 怒气被放下。

branches.en: A serious wrong is pardoned.
branches.cn: 严重的过错被宽恕。

branches.en: A debt is crossed out.
branches.cn: 债务被划掉。

branches.en: A polite word softens a request.
branches.cn: 礼貌用语让请求变柔和。

branches.en: Personal anger and public pardon share one release.
branches.cn: 私人怒气与公开赦免共享同一种释放。

intro.en: Forgive builds a family of pardon and patience words.
intro.cn: forgive 构成表示宽恕与耐心的词族。

latinIntro.en: Forgive is Germanic; Latin ignoscere, to pardon, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: forgive 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 ignoscere（宽恕）只是语义对应词。

definition_zh: 构成；算是；设立
definition_en: to form or make up something, or to establish it officially
core_image: 几块砖被摆成一个明确的形状，成为一堵墙
scene: 老师指着实验台上的几样器材说明用途。 These small parts constitute the whole system.
sceneCN: 这里 constitute 指「构成」（第 1 个义项：若干部分组成整体）；句意是这些小部件构成了整个系统。

senses.title: Make up a whole
senses.definition: to form a whole when the parts are taken together
senses.definitionCN: 各部分合起来形成一个整体
senses.example: Ten chapters constitute the whole book.
senses.exampleCN: 十章构成了整本书。
senses.why: A whole is only a name until its parts are counted.
senses.whyCN: 整体在数清部分之前，只是一个名字。

senses.title: Amount to something
senses.definition: to be serious or important enough to count as something
senses.definitionCN: 严重或重要到足以被算作某事
senses.example: Such neglect may constitute a crime.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疏忽可能构成犯罪。
senses.why: Law needs a line where a behaviour becomes a named act.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一条界线，让某种行为变成有名字的罪行。

senses.title: Set up officially
senses.definition: to establish an official body by formal act
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式程序建立官方机构
senses.example: They constituted a committee to study the case.
senses.exampleCN: 他们设立了一个委员会来研究此案。
senses.why: A group becomes an institution on the day it is written down.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体在被写下来的那天，才成为机构。

intro.en: Constitute comes from Latin constituere, to set up or appoint, built from com-, together, and statuere, to place.
intro.cn: constitute 来自拉丁语 constituere，意为设立或任命，由 com-（一起）与 statuere（放置）构成。

items.en: Statuere meant to set something in place and make it stand.
items.cn: statuere 意为把某物放好并让它立住。

items.en: Constituere meant to set up a body or appoint an officer.
items.cn: constituere 意为设立机构或任命官员。

items.en: The noun constitutio named an arrangement and later a decree.
items.cn: 名词 constitutio 指安排，后来指法令。

items.en: French constituer used the word for founding and composing.
items.cn: 法语 constituer 用它表示创立与组成。

items.en: English constitute meant to establish an official body.
items.cn: 英语 constitute 最初指设立官方机构。

items.en: It now commonly means to make up or amount to something.
items.cn: 如今它常表示构成或等同于某事。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin statu- base, and the meaning group names other verbs for making up a whole.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语 statu- 词基，近义组列出其他表示构成整体的动词。

entries.definition: the basic laws of a state, or the way something is made
entries.definitionCN: 宪法；构成

entries.definition: one of the parts that make up a whole
entries.definitionCN: 组成部分；成分

entries.definition: to start an official system or organization
entries.definitionCN: 设立；实行

entries.definition: to form the parts of a whole
entries.definitionCN: 组成；构成

entries.definition: to consist of particular parts
entries.definitionCN: 由…构成

entries.definition: to make something into a shape or body
entries.definitionCN: 形成；组成

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from bricks set into one wall, then move to an act heavy enough to count as a crime and to a body written into being.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从砌成一堵墙的砖开始，再到重到足以算作犯罪的行为，最后到被写出来的机构。

normal.en: Con- is together and stitute is set up, so constitute is setting things up into one body.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，stitute 是设立，constitute 就是把东西搭成一个整体。

normal.en: Bricks do not become a wall until they are counted together.
normal.cn: 砖要一起被数清，才变成一堵墙。

normal.en: A small act can constitute a big charge in a court.
normal.cn: 一个小动作，在法庭上可能构成重罪。

normal.en: To constitute a committee is to write a group into being.
normal.cn: 设立一个委员会，就是把一群人写进现实。

normal.en: First the parts, then the name of the whole.
normal.cn: 先有部分，再有整体的名字。

abstract.en: Picture several blocks locked into one clear shape.
abstract.cn: 想象几块积木扣成一个清晰的形状。

abstract.en: Picture a line of names signed under a new rule.
abstract.cn: 想象一条新规下面签着一排名字。

abstract.en: Picture one drop joining others to make a stream.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴水与其他水汇成一条小溪。

examples.en: Women constitute half of the workforce here.
examples.cn: 女性构成了这里劳动力的一半。

examples.en: Driving without lights may constitute an offence.
examples.cn: 不开灯驾驶可能构成违法。

examples.en: The members constituted a new council last spring.
examples.cn: 成员们在去年春天组建了一个新理事会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 constitute 记成 con（一起）加 stitute（设立）：把若干部分一起立起来，就成了一个整体，即构成。

root: 源自拉丁语 constituere（com 一起 + statuere 放置），本义是把东西一起立起来，后指构成整体、等同于某事与正式设立。

sensesIntro.en: From parts forming a whole, to an act serious enough to be named, and at last to a body set up by formal words.
sensesIntro.cn: 从部分形成整体，到严重到足以被命名的行为，最后到用正式文字设立的机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bricks set down one by one until a wall stands.
core.cn: 核心意象：砖一块块放好，直到一堵墙立起来。

branches.en: The first sense simply joins parts into one named whole.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只是把部分合成一个有名字的整体。

branches.en: The second sense says an act is heavy enough to be renamed as an offence.
branches.cn: 第二个义项说某行为重到可以被改称为一项罪名。

branches.en: The third sense writes a group into official existence.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把一个群体写进正式的建制。

branches.en: Both senses turn separate pieces into something with a legal name.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把分散的片段变成有正式名称的东西。

branches.en: A court and a council both depend on words that constitute.
branches.cn: 法庭与理事会都依靠那些起构成作用的文字。

intro.en: Constitute is built on Latin con-, together, plus statuere, to set in place.
intro.cn: constitute 由拉丁语 con-（一起）与 statuere（放置）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin set base stitut- also appears in constitution, institute and substitute.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的放置词基 stitut- 也出现在 constitution、institute 与 substitute 中。

items.meaning: to set parts up into one whole
items.example: These twelve poems constitute the collection.
items.exampleCN: 这十二首诗构成了这本诗集。

items.meaning: the way something is built, or a state's basic law
items.meaningCN: 构成方式，或国家的根本法

items.example: The court called the rule constitutional.
items.exampleCN: 法院认定该规定符合宪法。

items.meaning: one part that helps form a whole
items.example: Water is the main constituent of the drink.
items.exampleCN: 水是这种饮料的主要成分。

items.meaning: to set a system in place
items.example: They instituted a new safety rule.
items.exampleCN: 他们设立了一条新的安全规定。

items.meaning: a law set down in writing
a figure set up to stand
to put one thing in place of another
items.meaningCN: 把一物放到另一物的位置
items.example: You can substitute honey for sugar.
